# User scenarios and test gaps

NixOS machine integration tests and property-based tests are the preferred evidence. Unit tests establish narrower behavior. **Present** means a test exists and its assertion was inspected; **recorded** links a historical execution record, not a rerun of the current tree. Partial coverage does not mean the feature is broken. Gaps identify what the evidence cannot establish.

## Invite, retire and register a fresh identity with the same email

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Verified email identity, current elevated administrator, immediate account revocation and old-UUID cleanup through physical lifecycle fences.

Required refusal: Reject ordinary/self/mismatched retirement, pre-retirement links, copied revoked sessions and inherited credentials or grants; retain disk holds during busy or unavailable execution.

Tested scope: Historical 009 retirement/cleanup and the complete fourth extended NixOS journey on f4de549a retain their email-derived identity scope. Current database tests establish canonical reservations, migration and rollback. Original feature NixOS (484.07 seconds) and Ubuntu (541.14 seconds) generated-identity lifecycles passed retirement closure, fresh same-email/no inheritance, physical cleanup, retained shared GUID/PID, old-home reservation, explicit fresh sharing and packaged Lyra SSH. Those records apply to base 63a1443c plus feature f1bd0e05. Separate incoming d4499c4c merged eight-subtest lifecycle captures passed on NixOS438.33seconds and Ubuntu574.18seconds; they do not establish later browser-launcher/shared-observability integration.

- **machine, recorded**: [fresh same-email registration inherits nothing while old cleanup remains pinned](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/account-lifecycle/driver.py) — Separate feature f1bd0e05 plus incoming d4499c4c merged captures passed all eight subtests on NixOS438.33seconds and Ubuntu574.18seconds: real retirement, fresh same-email identity/no inheritance, pinned cleanup, retained shared storage/process/home, permanent old-home reservation and explicit fresh re-sharing. One disposable KVM failure domain; not later incoming source or complete Ubuntu SSH/editor acceptance.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-10-durable-guest-identities.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [retirement rejects an active team owner with a stable reason](repo:marshall/test/marshall/accounts/account_lifecycle_test.exs) — Base 63a1443c plus durable feature f1bd0e05, before incoming d4499c4c integration: Current focused lifecycle/Ingress 26-test rerun: a real team-owner refusal after GuestAccount retirement begins preserves the prior account marker/audit, active User and absent deletion receipt through transaction rollback.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-10-durable-guest-identities.md).
- **machine, present**: [lifecycle-refused-admission-retry](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/account-lifecycle/driver.py) — Present revised disposable fixture requires two real fresh enabled/execution-ready host/pool reports initially and one during the deliberate owned-host outage. It retries only exact closed insufficient_capacity with unchanged request key and bounded deadline; accepted/unknown outcomes stop. Both native witnesses passed creation under real admission, without fabricating telemetry/capacity; the refusal-retry branch is not separately forced..
- **machine, present**: [lifecycle-independent-shared-transport](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/account-lifecycle/driver.py) — Present corrected fixture resolves co-location through authorized public relocation, waits complete/finished plus running/current destination and requires distinct hosts before GUID/PID capture and owned-host fault. **Gaps:** Both original feature witnesses and incoming d4499c4c merged witnesses passed after correcting setup co-location/transfer enrollment and the shared-delete oracle for legitimate relocation source cleanup. Arbitrary interruption points, independent physical-host failures, hardware authenticators, live SMTP and later incoming integration remain separate.

**Preferred test work:** Retain both serial generated-identity lifecycle results and historical email-derived evidence at their actual scopes. Extend native arbitrary-interruption and independent physical-host schedules; preserve real admission/reservations and live shared-stream/home witnesses. Real SMTP and hardware authenticator acceptance remain distinct.

## Save separate launch, machine and thread creation presets and create or replay a machine

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Accounts stores only the authenticated actor’s three independent groups. Browser forms seed matching initial values; Compute remains admission authority. An admitted launch reuses its original owner/key request before source-checked admission.

Required refusal: Malformed sizes, forbidden profiles, disabled or source-incapable launch images, foreign target identifiers and revoked logins cannot persist defaults. Explicit machine drafts remain subject to ordinary admission.

Tested scope: ADR-0240 account persistence, preset isolation, browser form seeding, draft retention, source fallback and original-request launch replay in the BEAM test VM.

- **unit, recorded**: [three presets persist independently and seed their creation surfaces](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/machine_defaults_test.exs) — Self-only persisted groups, default profiles, independent forms and draft refresh/reload in real LiveViews with sandboxed PostgreSQL.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-account-machine-presets.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [settings reject invalid defaults and revoked logins without changing any preset](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/machine_defaults_test.exs) — Typed save-action refusals and mounted-page revoked-login refusal without account mutation.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-account-machine-presets.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [launch uses its saved profile and sizes and replay keeps the original request](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/machine_defaults_test.exs) — Ordinary Compute admission, immutable source and VM identity after changed account preferences; owner isolation of original-request projection.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-account-machine-presets.md).
- **property, recorded**: [profile drafts survive refresh and reload before duplicate submission](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/default_profile_history_test.exs) — Generated omitted/explicit browser profiles, refresh, reload, stable key and duplicate admission; current omitted profile is Standard.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-account-machine-presets.md).
- **machine, present**: [stage = "account machine preset"](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/default-oss/browser.py) — Packaged native browser fixture saves an OSS preset, reloads settings and retains it through creation/reload before existing guest policy probes. Revised source is present; execution pending..
- **manual, recorded**: [id="machine-defaults"](repo:marshall/lib/marshall_web/live/account_live.ex) — Disposable real Chromium: independent saves/reloads, matching machine/thread initial values, 36 route/locale/theme/viewport combinations (settings and both create forms; English/Arabic/Japanese; light/dark; 1440/390 px), grid, overflow, direction, primary font, contrast and same-origin/CSP. Inspected representative screenshots; no guest execution or independent linguistic acceptance.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-account-machine-presets.md).

**Gaps:** Native guest execution, real-browser layout beyond English/Arabic/Japanese, cross-node first-admission preference races and production migration/rollout remain unverified. Existing isolation and storage evidence retains its original scope.

**Preferred test work:** Execute the revised NixOS default-profile journey that saves an OSS preset, and extend it to all three preset forms and an actual thread/launch. Add generated preference-update/replay interleavings across independent nodes.

## Open the single account page, move between its profile, sign-in, SSH key, Git and machine-default sections, and reach it from the sidebar, the step-up redirect, the SSH approval page and the CLI hint

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport.

Boundary: One LiveView at /settings mounts through the AuthenticationPrivacy tag and LiveUserAuth's :security mode, so the profile, passkey, SSH key, Git and machine-default sections all recheck the persisted login on mount, every event, every message and every parameter change; mutations use the socket actor through User.security, Marshall.SSH, User.set_time_zone, User.git_settings and User.save_machine_defaults; fragments (#profile, #security, #ssh-keys, #git-settings, #machine-defaults) carry no authority and return_to keeps its allowlist.

Required refusal: Refuse anonymous visitors with a sign-in redirect; answer 404 on /settings/profile, /settings/security and /settings/ssh-keys; refuse unknown events with a fixed flash and no change; a revoked login halts the next SSH key event or clock tick with a sign-in redirect; a weaker mount (optional, current_user or none) fails the pin test.

Tested scope: LiveView tests of the merged page (sections, single navigation entry, the step-up redirect and Users link to /settings?return_to=%2Fadmin%2Fusers#security, the SSH approval confirmation, which stays on the approval page with the Open Mila link (ADR-0221) rather than navigating to /settings#ssh-keys, every former Security, SSH key and profile assertion) and a structural pin of the lifecycle ids and route; the synthetic browser probe checks the single sidebar entry, section order, anchors landing at the top, the zone round trip and grid alignment in both themes and at 390 px.

- **unit, present**: [the merged page keeps the strict security mount of the former Security page](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/account_live_test.exs) — Exact lifecycle mount ids [{AuthenticationPrivacy, :default}, {LiveUserAuth, :security}] and the /settings route to AccountLive.
- **unit, present**: [the page renders every section behind one Account navigation entry](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/account_live_test.exs) — All five section ids and index anchors, #nav-account current, #nav-usage, no /settings/* sidebar links, the account-menu clock link to /settings#profile.
- **unit, present**: [anonymous visitors must sign in and the old settings pages are gone](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/account_live_test.exs) — Sign-in redirect on /settings and 404 on the three removed paths.
- **unit, present**: [admin reads remain available but a mutation prompts step-up](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/account_live_test.exs) — The no-key administrator redirect and the Users page link target /settings?return_to=%2Fadmin%2Fusers#security.
- **unit, present**: [revoked browser login cannot change keys through an existing LiveView](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/account_live_test.exs) — A revoked persisted token halts the SSH key event on the merged page with a sign-in redirect and no key is stored.
- **manual, present**: [check_account](repo:marshall/scripts/monospace_browser_probe.py) — Current synthetic browser fixture targets the Account route and all five sections, retains Git preference and zone round trips, anchor positioning, grid alignment and light/dark/mobile screenshots. Source and static checks do not record browser execution of this repaired probe..

**Gaps:** The NixOS browser tests, the passkey probe and the Antithesis access workload were rewritten to /settings by inspection and have not been executed against the merged page; no property test fits a page composition.

**Preferred test work:** Rerun the credential-self-service, mfa-login, admin-account, account-lifecycle, control-room and fleet Porsche browser machine tests on the merged page and record them; rerun the Antithesis access workload.

## Read the Control room without administrative mutation authority

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization.

Boundary: Signed-in read access is separate from administrator membership plus fresh elevation.

Required refusal: Reject forged mutation events and forged administrator flags from ordinary users.

Tested scope: Generated and fixed current-role/elevation/stored-login histories through actual Ash actions, mounted LiveViews and exports; recorded native browser scenario with virtual WebAuthn. Campaign 015 separately checks the packaged standalone browser helper with pinned ty; recorded native execution retains its original source and scope.

- **property, present**: [removing the owning entity attribute never preserves Cedar authority](repo:marshall/test/marshall/authorization/cedar_test.exs) — Generated VM, team and integration owner actions against the real Cedar evaluator; valid controls allow and resources missing their owner attribute refuse. This does not inject a database fault or prove an Ash authorizer caller boundary.

- **machine, recorded**: [native-control-room-authority](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/control-room/browser.py) — Current native nine-page admin inventory, ordinary reader access, virtual WebAuthn elevation, forged role-write refusal and unchanged audit/role state, revocation, demotion, mounted login expiry and export404. Real sign-out removes remembered custody before fresh-request refusal; one serving replica.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-09-observability-decoupling.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [native-subsequent-mfa-login](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/mfa-login/browser.py) — Three colocated serving replicas, virtual WebAuthn, subsequent magic-link and remembered login, actual backend and WebSocket observations, admin-UI mounted/copied-cookie revocation including a no-MFA account.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-mfa-login-verification.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [administrative revocation on one replica refuses every protected read on the others](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/cross_replica_revocation_test.exs) — Three independent BEAM instances sharing committed PostgreSQL; mounted Control room, handbook and machine read checks, the mounted usage export and the account projection read action all refuse after revocation committed on another replica; commit-boundary race and partition fail-closed with rejoin enforcement. **Preferred test work:** Populate native drill-down pages and remaining administrative mutation families; retain cross-replica browser session revocation and current-role properties.

## Reset an account and refuse administrative mutations after elevation or role loss

Coverage: **covered**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, recovery.

Boundary: Current stored browser login, administrator role and fixed passkey elevation retained through account mutation and audit commit; retirement keeps its exclusive admission fence before sorted participants.

Required refusal: Reject stale mounted/domain role, global-session, reset, invitation and retirement mutations after authority loss without target, token, credential, outbox/job, deletion or audit changes.

Tested scope: Five real account action families with independent generated histories and 27 passing three-Marshall schedules; captured packaged-browser reset and five stale-page refusals pass with verified TLS and virtual WebAuthn.

- **property, recorded**: [admin-account-history-oracle](repo:marshall/test/marshall/accounts/admin_account_history_test.exs) — Five generated histories call real actions and compare independent permission/target models and complete refusal inventories.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-admin-account-authority-verification.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [completed revocation refuses fresh mutations on every peer without a gate](repo:marshall/test/marshall/accounts/admin_account_distributed_test.exs) — 27 schedules use three independent BEAMs and real PostgreSQL, audit-write gates, sorted consumers, admission fences and peer-side completion; no native guest assertion.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-admin-account-authority-verification.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [native-admin-account-authority](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/admin-account/browser.py) — One packaged Marshall with verified TLS, virtual WebAuthn, real same-login lock and second-admin role demotion; target reset and five individual stale-page refusals.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-admin-account-authority-verification.md).

**Gaps:** Hardware authenticators, independent physical hosts, SMTP delivery and production rollout remain separate; full/native captures and previous Control room/retirement claims retain their exact revisions.

**Preferred test work:** Preferred property and native evidence is recorded for the stated scope. Physical authenticator/host and SMTP/provider acceptance requires separately provisioned infrastructure.

## Approve a packaged agent CLI invocation in an ordinary browser and receive real guest work

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation.

Boundary: Explicit current browser approval binds an in-memory secret digest to one actor and VM for one hour; every API checks current account/write access and exact thread binding, then ordinary model and guest execution fences apply.

Required refusal: GET and digest URLs cannot approve/authenticate; stale sharing or browser login refuses approval. Existing CLI requests refuse withdrawn write access, retired account, deleted VM, expiry, foreign IDs or changed request payload. Browser sign-out alone does not revoke an independently approved CLI session.

Tested scope: Independent generated direct/team authority and invocation histories plus a dedicated native ordinary-browser, packaged-CLI, real stopped guest and deterministic provider journey.

- **property, recorded**: [generated approval sequences keep one session per digest with classified refusals](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/agent_revocation_history_test.exs) — Repeated, fresh and owner/member digests after withdrawal; expired rows are removed once and live rows persist across another sweep. SQL-backed fixture only.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-29-antithesis-property-audit.md).
- **property, recorded**: [CLI invocations follow direct and team authority histories](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/agent_cli_history_test.exs) — Public HTTP/LiveView calls after actual sharing/team actions; full persisted-row refusal inventories, fresh digest approvals, exact retry and binding controls, guaranteed expiry/deletion/retirement boundaries and independent browser logout semantics. Synthetic capacity/execution fixtures are control evidence only.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-agent-cli-verification.md).
- **property, recorded**: [browser sign-out and CLI expiry have separate authority boundaries](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/agent_cli_history_test.exs) — Expiry, deletion and retirement remain present in every generated and shrunk lifetime permutation. Reproduced duplicate-exhaustion seed 605897 now runs the actual HTTP/LiveView and SQL-backed assertions; synthetic capacity/execution fixtures remain application evidence only.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-26-cli-history-generator.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [browser GET cannot approve and explicit consent completes packaged CLI guest work](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/agent-cli-journey/driver.py) — Ordinary member browser sign-in and explicit digest approval; packaged CLI against verified HTTPS; real Marshall/Ziggy/Audi/Lilly/NixOS guest wake, model/tool/final response; child capability refusal and mounted stale approval after owner UI sharing withdrawal. Nine NixOS machines on one physical KVM host; isolated provider.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-25-agent-cli-verification.md).

**Gaps:** Native attempt two's executor interruption remains unexplained; the passing capture predates the subsequent Underclass package pin. Independent physical hosts, production providers/load/rollout, Ubuntu browser-approved CLI and native hostile-tool/profile permutations remain separate. Inception verification is excluded by user direction.

**Preferred test work:** Follow-up 030 adds composed dispatch histories and a native started-effect fixture. Establish native pre-start observation before claiming that case; preserve the earlier unexplained interruption.

## Continue a long thread through automatic or requested context compaction

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Agents owns immutable context snapshots and covered-prefix checkpoints independently of retained transcript events. Existing Ziggy admission/accounting and current generation/frontier checks govern model effects and publication. Eligible-turn coverage must exclude queued later prompts and include accepted continuation exactly once.

Required refusal: Refuse oversized required instructions/current input, orphaned tool groups, stale or incomplete checkpoint results and no-progress compaction. Unknown native capability uses summary mode. A generated summary cannot change trusted mode or permissions. Ambiguous claimed model calls cannot be replayed automatically.

Tested scope: Pure compaction tests, generated complete-tool-group coverage and a distributed process-loss reconstruction fixture are present. The distributed fixture stops the admitting peer and reconstructs the checkpoint and compaction plan from committed PostgreSQL state through replacement peers; it does not run a guest or provider.

- **property, present**: [completed tool groups are either entirely summarized or entirely retained](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/compaction_test.exs) — Generated pure request groups assert that compaction does not split a completed function call from its result; no database or provider execution is included..
- **unit, present**: [only bounded completed purpose-specific output can become a checkpoint](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/compaction_test.exs) — Pure completion validation rejects malformed or incomplete summary/native output before checkpoint publication..
- **unit, present**: [unknown native support uses tool-free summaries and keeps instructions outside generated state](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/compaction_test.exs) — Pure request construction selects the summary fallback without verified native support and preserves separate trusted instructions..
- **unit, recorded**: [a compaction plan can be reconstructed by another process after worker loss](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/agent_context_recovery_distributed_test.exs) — The distributed fixture stops the compaction worker and reconstructs the checkpoint and plan through a replacement peer using committed PostgreSQL state; no guest or provider is involved.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-16-agent-context-and-planning.md).

**Gaps:** SQL checkpoint publication races, queued-prompt interleaving, native Marshall-to-Ziggy/provider/guest composition and live provider capability acceptance remain unverified. Process-peer recovery observes committed state but does not establish independent-host or guest recovery.

**Preferred test work:** Execute generated SQL checkpoint/replay histories and a NixOS Marshall-to-Ziggy-to-provider-fixture-to-guest continuation including claim loss, stale completion and repeated compaction; verify live native compaction separately before enabling it.

## Inspect uncertain guest work and explicitly retry with current CLI authority

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: Current browser/CLI authority, durable command start, VM placement and executor fence; exact disposable guest process interruption.

Required refusal: Refuse expired/replaced executor results and revoked CLI use; never redispatch an uncertain command or turn an identical request replay into new work.

Tested scope: Composed generated application histories plus a strict native started-effect fixture with real packaged CLI and source-built guest; recorded executions are captured at the staged branch tree.

- **property, present**: [preserves one dispatch and explicit retry](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/executor_loss_history_test.exs) — Eight separate 100-case property runners cover claimed/started loss, replacement/synthetic expiry and allowed/revoked access, with repeated polling, stale transitions, request identity, sharing withdrawal/regrant and an unrelated workload inventory in each case. The former shuffled combined runner's execution record remains historical. Current runner execution is present only; synthetic SQL control evidence cannot establish native effects..
- **machine, recorded**: [real started effect is frozen before targeted executor and child loss](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/executor-loss/driver.py) — Ordinary marvin/packaged CLI, real Standard guest effect, external cgroup observer, exact executor/child fault and actual replacement fence, explicit retry and UI revocation. Pre-start native loss is excluded.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-26-executor-loss-histories.md).

**Gaps:** Native pre-start loss has no safe identified observation seam; application histories use synthetic running receipts/expiry and model results. The recorded native run is one started-effect interruption on one staged tree. Earlier native CLI attempt two remains unexplained. Physical hosts, Ubuntu, live providers, native expiry histories and long-duration replay absence remain separate.

**Preferred test work:** Retain native pre-start interruption as follow-up until its observation seam is established; rerun the strict driver after agent executor, fence or helper contract changes.

## Apply the thread creator's guest and project guidance with explicitly selected skills

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Verified source digests and complete selected skill bodies enter immutable snapshots; Marshall host files and a collaborator's personal configuration are not sources. Required refusal: Refuse unsafe linked instruction paths, stale digests, malformed chunks, nonexistent creator profiles, stale execution and required content beyond context limits. ## Plan work, answer durable questions and implement the exact completed proposal

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Persisted Plan/Work collaboration is trusted application state separate from reasoning. Root Plan turns own durable questions and the first current authorized answer. A completed proposal binds one Work turn on the same thread and machine. Plan is instructional and does not create a read-only filesystem boundary.

Required refusal: Viewers and revoked actors cannot answer or implement. Child agents cannot ask human questions. Stale, cancelled, archived or nonactive requests refuse. Tested scope: Pure proposal/question tests, a generated truncated-proposal property, SQL-backed persistence cases and a distributed process-loss fixture are present. No hosted or physical-power-loss proof.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-13-antithesis-harness-foundation.md).

**Gaps:** No physical power-loss durability, KVM/Firecracker behavior, production reverse-path validation, real guest attribution, composed container startup or hosted Antithesis baseline. Preferred native machine/property coverage remains separate.

**Preferred test work:** Run native NixOS ZFS/router machine and generated recovery properties at the selected source, then validate the container entrypoint and hosted graph independently.

## An agent publishes an artifact, revises it with read-before-write, the owner shares it with a viewer who renders it on the isolated content origin, and revoking the share stops the viewer's next fetch

## Open the overview or machine list and see exactly the machines and controls current authority allows, without per-machine authorization latency

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Machine pages (overview, list, pinned section, get, resolve) read through Compute.Views in one outermost REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction. Inside it the persisted Cedar principal, owners, grant, thread and team rows, entities and projection rows are read once or in identical batches and dropped when the transaction ends; Cedar still evaluates every row. Nested in another transaction nothing is reused.

Required refusal: Omit any machine a fresh per-row read decision refuses, project the same read/write/manage permissions fresh decisions return, hide a revoked machine on the next read, and never reuse a read across refreshes, requests or processes.

Tested scope: Generated grant roles through the real Compute.list_vms action and Access.set_access against local PostgreSQL, fresh Access.Authorization decisions as the oracle, revocation between reads and a query budget. No native journey.

- **property, recorded**: [batched pages make the same decisions as fresh per-row checks](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/views_batched_reads_test.exs) — Generated viewer, operator, manager and revoked roles for one member over four owned machines against local PostgreSQL in the SQL sandbox (memoization active, isolation level not changeable there); [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [a revoked grant disappears on the next page read](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/views_batched_reads_test.exs) — Manager grant listed, revoked between two list reads, omitted on the second read; no batch remains active between reads; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [page queries do not grow with additional machines](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/views_batched_reads_test.exs) — Owner list query count with four and twelve unrelocated machines in the SQL sandbox; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [catalog queries do not grow with eligible hosts](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/views_batched_reads_test.exs) — Catalog query count with two and six fresh hosts in the SQL sandbox; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [outermost batches are repeatable-read and read-only; nested batches do not memoize](repo:marshall/test/marshall/authorization/decision_snapshot_isolation_test.exs) — Unboxed local PostgreSQL connection reports repeatable read and read-only, refuses an UPDATE, and a batch nested in a read-committed transaction does not memoize; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [creation form edits do not reload page data but a tick does](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/machines_live_test.exs) — Three validate edits on /machines/new emit no page refresh; one tick emits exactly one; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [probe, physical stop, full copy, import and readiness](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/relocation_sources_test.exs) — Batched and listed relocation status, including ongoing and finished downtime from a recorded pause outcome and destination readiness, equal the per-row read; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-22-liveview-load-performance.md).

**Gaps:** Concurrent revocation during a refresh is argued from snapshot semantics, not observed. The list query plan was measured on synthetic fleet-sized data, not production data. No native browser journey measures page latency.

**Preferred test work:** Add a NixOS machine test that loads /machines with many shared machines and checks the marshall.live.refresh query_count.

## Find the browser extension guide, download an unsigned launcher and explicitly configure its server before a provider click

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Public and signed-in navigation and Overview link to the canonical public /docs/browser-extension guide. Guidance grants no identity or compute authority. Marshall serves a closed artifact allowlist from a canonical immutable Nix-store package over its existing public HTTPS boundary without login state; operators may disable downloads while the guide remains public. Strict native modules transmit only provider origin/path after removing source queries/fragments, only after an explicit provider toolbar click to an explicitly configured origin. The configured extension requests optional access only for that exact Overalls origin and marks the open page with a local installed signal; Marshall uses that signal only to hide setup affordances. Public package possession and the marker grant no compute authority; the repository-launch scenario owns authenticated capture and admission.

Required refusal: Disabled downloads, mutable/traversing roots, symlink root/bin/file, malformed descriptors, length mismatch, missing files and unknown artifacts return404. Missing or malformed server settings open options without transmitting. Known unsupported URLs disable the action. Withheld URLs preserve the explicit activeTab grant without transmitting; clicks validate the observed provider URL before opening Overalls. Source query/fragment fields are removed before transmission and URL user information refuses. Remote HTTP and credential-bearing server URLs refuse. Unsigned developer archives do not imply permanent Firefox installation. A denied or withdrawn exact-origin permission, failed registration, missing configuration or unavailable detector leaves setup visible; a spoofed marker never authorizes a request.

Tested scope: Present controller/LiveView assertions inspect the canonical guide's two downloads, unsigned Chrome and temporary Firefox setup wording, public navigation and signed-in Overview CTA; no new real-browser discovery/setup execution is recorded. Recorded final strict typing/10 Node tests, deterministic minimized immutable package/check, real Chromium and exact immutable Firefox four-provider sentinel action clicks producing only origin/path launch URLs, unknown-URL click refusal, settings/metadata, developer/store byte equality and host immutable-download refusals. Exact-origin detector source and package assertions are being added; Chrome and Firefox setup-visibility runtime evidence remains pending. Firefox uses fixed local TLS/certificate bypass; installed-extension auth/guest composition and production downloads remain separate.

## Open Marshall in a browser and receive the same strict security headers, no-index directives and host-prefixed cookies on every response

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: MarshallWeb.SecurityHeaders sets one Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self' plus 'wasm-unsafe-eval' for the terminal sixel decoder, ADR-0230; style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline' for the vendored xterm.js and Mermaid renderers), Permissions-Policy, same-origin opener and resource policies, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN framing and no cross-domain policies before health, static files, the early /api refusals and the router. MarshallWeb.NoIndex adds X-Robots-Tag on the same surfaces and the root layout repeats it as a robots meta tag beside the disallow-all robots.txt. Production sends HSTS max-age=63072000 with includeSubDomains and no preload. The production session cookie is __Host-marshall (Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, no Domain, SameSite=Lax, signed and encrypted) and the remembered credential is __Host-remember_me; MarshallWeb.BrowserSession owns the options for Plug.Session, the LiveView socket and every forged-session test or release probe, and expires legacy cookie names carried by a request. Headers and cookies grant nothing: stored-login checks, Cedar and CSRF tokens decide access, and user applications on *.apps.ghuntley.dev remain same-site with Marshall.

Required refusal: Inline, foreign or evaluated script, plugins, foreign frames, form targets outside self and the fixed https://ghuntley.com newsletter fallback origin, and cross-site framing of Marshall are refused by the browser; unrestricted https: is not a form source. A __Host- cookie set by a sibling origin or without Secure/Path=/ is dropped; the test build refuses development-tooling policy sources; a route may tighten but never duplicate a header.

Tested scope: Unit tests assert the exact header set on a rendered page, the signed-out redirect, a static file, the health probe, a refused /api path and a JSON API reply, the production versus development policy strings, the :secure and :plain session options through Plug.Session including encryption and legacy-name expiry, and the __Host-remember_me Set-Cookie attributes issued by a real magic-link sign-in. Covenant obligations I7 and I8 repeat the header and cookie invariants. The Playwright probe asserts the strict policy header on every navigation and fails on any securitypolicyviolation or Chromium CSP console report; it recorded zero violations through the owner routes in both themes and the thread views before stopping on pre-existing thread layout findings unrelated to the headers.

- **unit, recorded**: [every response surface carries the fixed header set once](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/security_headers_test.exs) — Page, redirect, static file, health, refused /api path and JSON API reply carry the exact header values exactly once; development additions and the strict production script-src are checked as strings.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-marshall-security-headers.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [secure mode issues an encrypted __Host- cookie with the required attributes](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/browser_session_test.exs) — Plug.Session round trip under the :secure options, signing-only reader refusal, :plain development options and legacy remember_me expiry only when the request carries it.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-marshall-security-headers.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [assert_host_prefixed_remember_cookie(response, name)](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/remember_me_login_test.exs) — A real magic-link sign-in with remember enabled issues __Host-remember_me with path=/, secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, a max-age and no Domain.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-marshall-security-headers.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [every browser endpoint response asks search engines not to index](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/public_endpoint_test.exs) — X-Robots-Tag on the root redirect, sign-in page, robots.txt, health and a refused /api path, plus the robots meta tag on the rendered sign-in page.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-marshall-security-headers.md).
- **manual, present**: [presentation-no-csp-violations](repo:marshall/scripts/monospace_browser_probe.py) — Chromium 151 with Playwright 1.59 against the disposable fixture: strict policy header on every navigation, zero CSP violations through the owner routes in both themes and the thread views; the run stopped on pre-existing thread layout findings, so the final evidence line was not printed..

**Gaps:** No NixOS machine test asserts the headers, HSTS or cookie attributes over the packaged release and TLS proxy, and the production deployment has not been observed sending them. The credential-rotation and mfa-login machine tests were not re-run after the cookie rename. The browser probe did not reach its final evidence line because of a two-pixel thread-workspace grid offset and a thread-activity overflow that reproduce with CSP bypassed. User applications stay same-site with the control plane, so SameSite gives no CSRF protection against them.

**Preferred test work:** Add a NixOS browser machine assertion for the header set, HSTS and the __Host- cookies over the packaged release, re-run the credential-rotation and mfa-login machine tests, and fix the thread layout findings so the probe completes. A generated-policy property adds nothing over the fixed header strings.

## Clone a machine without sharing its mutable disk

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Snapshot ownership, audit and current requester authority, serialized publication/cancellation, immutable snapshot, source restoration and independently proven cleanup.

Required refusal: Refuse withdrawn manager actions and queued activation, changed request inputs, cancelled retries and cancellation after publication; retain unknown cleanup holds. Retain transfer slots until both endpoint revocation receipts; retain the source snapshot hold, the source exclusion and the prune offer through cleanup uncertainty and past the cleanup deadline; refuse stale recovery over newer source intent. Malformed clone control JSON receives a permanent 400 invalid_message before host state changes. Reject a clone or relocation claim while the host transfer slot is occupied.

Independent upstream histories and native owned-staging evidence retain their recorded scope. ## Keep a live guest SSH session through lilly-hostd and Lilly restarts while Lilly can still end it

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, transport, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: ADR-0187. After guardian admission the BEAM sends Audi's accepted connection to hostd (op 14). hostd accepts only a connected AF_UNIX stream whose peer uid is Audi's, dials the guest in the VM namespace, and starts lilly-ingress-bridge --detached as lilly in its own lilly-ingress-<key>.scope in lilly_ingress.slice, outside lilly-hostd.service and lilly.service; the ready frame is written before any guest byte. Lilly records the binding under the key first, keeps an ingress guardian per bridge, and ends the bridge through hostd (op 16) when that guardian dies.

Required refusal: hostd refuses a BridgeIngress descriptor that is not Audi's connected, non-listening AF_UNIX stream, a 1025th bridge or a reused key, and lists or kills only lilly-ingress-<32 hex>.scope cgroups in its slice. A restarted Lilly ends a live bridge without a readable record at once and a recorded one whose execution is not current within 30 s; a bridge hostd abandons before GO moves no byte. Marshall answers SSH renewal while Lilly reconnects with unavailable only after key, owner, write membership, VM state, generation and session checks, so key removal, revoked write access and a stop stay conclusive; admission still needs a live, reported host.

Tested scope: hostd Hegel decoding and scope-name models, fake-cgroup list/end, the client check and the start handshake with a fake helper; bridge Hegel command-line oracle and handshake process fixture; Lilly connector tests with a fake host for handoff, guardian-death fencing and re-adoption. Marshall SSH renewal across a simulated Lilly reconnect and Audi SSH channel retry of an unavailable renewal. No scope, VM namespace or real restart in these tests.

- **property, recorded**: [ingress_decoding_matches_model](repo:lilly/native/hostd/src/ingress_tests.rs) — Ops 14 to 16 against an independent decoding model, scope names round-trip, list and end over fake cgroups, Audi-only client check and the READY/greeting/GO start with a fake helper.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-detached-ingress-bridges.md).
- **property, recorded**: [command_line_matches_the_independent_oracle](repo:lilly/native/ingress-bridge/src/tests.rs) — The --detached command line against an independent oracle; the process fixture shows no guest byte before GO and an abandoned bridge moving none.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-detached-ingress-bridges.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [a restarted connector re-adopts recorded bridges and ends unknown ones](repo:lilly/test/ingress_bridges_test.exs) — Connector handoff, record before start, keeper fencing on guardian death, re-adoption, unknown and unadoptable bridges against a fake host.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-detached-ingress-bridges.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [SSH renewal across a Lilly restart is inconclusive, then keeps the binding](repo:marshall/test/marshall/ingress/sessions_test.exs) — Real SSH session authority: after a host disconnect and a new unreported session, renewal is temporarily_unavailable and admission is refused; after the first report renewal keeps the exact binding. Key removal, a viewer downgrade and a stop with a newer generation stay conclusive while reconnecting.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [unavailable SSH renewals during a Lilly restart are retried and the stream survives](repo:audi/test/ssh_transport_test.exs) — A fixture backend answers renewals with the class Audi maps Marshall's unavailable to, then allows; the SSH channel keeps the stream and carries it past its original deadline.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [live guest SSH survives lilly-hostd and Lilly restarts until its bridge is fenced](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/fleet/scenarios/user-ssh-journey.py) — Restart lilly-hostd, then Lilly, under a live guest SSH session: the same lilly-ingress-bridge process in its lilly-ingress-<key>.scope, a new hostd, echoed lines both ways, adoption logged and the session alive past the 30 s grace; then remove the record and restart Lilly: the session and scope end, the guest keeps its boot and a new session reconnects.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-detached-ingress-bridges.md).

**Gaps:** Editor and nested HTTPS moved to this path under ADR-0192 (staged-detached-ingress-survival). While Lilly is down no keeper runs, so a revoked execution's live session can last the downtime plus 30 s (Audi's key revocation is unaffected). The adoption grace is measured only on the test host. Until 2026-10-17 Marshall refused SSH renewal while Lilly reconnected, so a session whose renewal fell in the restart window was cut despite its bridge; the recorded machine run's renewals missed that window, and no machine run yet forces a renewal into it.

**Preferred test work:** Measure the adoption grace on a loaded production host.

## Discover editor and neutral webview origins only through gateways with matching immutable assets

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: transport, execution, storage.

Boundary: Ingress EditorAssetsReceipt binds each approved target's full release tuple independently to current host session/service generation. Every advertised editor/webview gateway must hold the complete configured set because neutral DNS cannot route by release; discovery remains separate from personal Editor admission.

Required refusal: Withhold editor/webview records when any configured target lacks a live five-second matching receipt or the current route is unhealthy. A tuple approved only for the other image target grants no capability. Refuse malformed/foreign/duplicate registry entries, wrong release, service role, stale credentials, unknown paths, symlinks and unsafe asset methods.

Tested scope: Recorded before integration with main independent-observability revision: SQL-backed publication tests passed in the 52-check focused run. Audi path-selection property and actual verified local TLS readiness/suspension passed in its final 197-check full component gate; native public DNS/TLS and multi-gateway publisher histories remain separate.

## An operator rotates a fleet public address by changing one SOPS document, and Marshall reaches Susan on salopettes over fleet0

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, execution, isolation, storage, recovery, transport.

Boundary: Fleet public addresses live only in secrets/fleet-addresses.enc.json; overalls-fleet-addresses validates every value before the runtime firewall chain, WireGuard endpoints, uplink drop-in and service binds use it; Overalls admits salopettes' handshake only from its decrypted address and resolves notifications.overalls.dev to 10.90.0.3.

Required refusal: A missing, malformed or wildcard address keeps every runtime rule, endpoint and listener closed; a rotation flushes before admitting; an unreadable document leaves a dedicated host on its root-only uplink recovery copy; static IPv4 address or route literals beside a runtime uplink are refused at evaluation.

Tested scope: NixOS machine tests on both firewall backends with test VLAN addresses, the fleet-network runtime-endpoint subtest, the proxy and relay socket runtime-address test, and evaluation of the fleet firewall, host planning and service modules.

Test VLAN addresses only.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-fleet-addresses-from-sops.md).

## Build on Panterloons or Dungarees and have the derivation scheduled by Panterloons' tribuchet hub onto either host's worker, with peer substitution over grpc://

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Panterloons alone runs the hub and has no build machines; Dungarees delegates only to Panterloons' mTLS grpc:// store. Tribuchet workers need a tribuchet-CA leaf; grpc peers need build-NAME from a separate CA, with trusted only for Dungarees on Panterloons and read-only the other way. Listeners are reachable only through tailscale0; keys come from per-host SOPS bundles; global signature checks stay for other substituters (ADR-0248).

Required refusal: An unmatched grpc CN is denied, the read-only peer cannot open the worker-protocol tunnel or import unsigned paths, and a worker certificate from another CA fails the hub handshake. With the hub or the scheduler's grpc daemon down, builds run locally instead of failing.

Tested scope: Final-tree two-VM machine check with fixture CAs on a plain VM network, plus an evaluation check on the real host configurations. No tailnet, deployment receipt, physical-host load or long-running soak is covered.

## Build Arch Linux and AlmaLinux images through the existing Linux guest contract

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Arch Linux and AlmaLinux use the version-4 kernel image shape with distinct pinned distribution roots and identities. Owned key-only SSH policy, pinned PAM modules and a requisite private login receipt preserve the existing Audi authority. Collision-checked locked sshd/overalls-ssh identities, files-only account lookup and pinned account command paths preserve roster custody. Root-owned regular setuid sudo uses only reconciler-managed per-user grants; vendor sshd enablement resolves to the readiness-gated listener. The root-only argument-free helper oneshot installs exact pinned immutable unix_chkpwd bytes at its compiled path before SSH, requiring regular root-owned source/destination and safe root-owned parents. Existing nosuid mounts remain; the pinned root PAM caller sets real UID 0 before helper execution. Marshall authorization, current-boot readiness, host isolation and native storage remain independent existing boundaries.

Required refusal: Missing distribution/contract inputs or malformed, colliding or exhausted system-account allocations refuse assembly. Helper arguments, nonroot callers, symlink/foreign/writable parents or unsafe source/destination custody refuse installation; SSH requires helper success. Isolated root-account checks preserve expired, password-change and unknown-account refusals. No password/root SSH path or vendor policy may replace the owned listener; absent current roster/login authority must refuse guest access. Evaluation and allocator tests do not establish live roster/revocation refusals or general distribution-native runtime support.

Tested scope: Evaluation inspects separate pinned roots, version-4 manifests, agent closure, owned SSH/PAM/account/sudo assembly and fixed ext4 inputs. Historical same-builder rootfs comparisons passed; a later cross-host Arch comparison failed because store-optimisation hardlinks changed inode allocation. Root and closure copying now discard incidental hardlinks. Final fleet-context Arch and Alma rootfs outputs then passed actual cross-host --check rebuild comparisons after signed cache substitution; exact derivations, outputs and limits are in the matrix review. Allocator fixtures cover malformed records, collisions, exhaustion and idempotence without booting either distribution.

Nosuid runtime mounts remain observed; no direct helper setuid elevation, roster revocation or broader guest-capability/isolation result.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).

## See where a guest boot spends its time and boot faster without weakening boot-bound trust

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, transport, recovery.

Boundary: The host boot-log writer stamps console lines without interpreting payloads under its 1 MiB cap; the guest boot report is observation only. Ubuntu skips update-ca-certificates only when the marker, managed root bytes, bundle PEM blocks and per-root links prove the store already reflects the exact delivered set; every boot still delivers and verifies the current host set before networking (ADR-0113, ADR-0154).

Required refusal: Any marker mismatch, changed, extra or missing managed root, missing bundle block or link, or failed rebuild takes the full replace path: the marker is withdrawn before mutation and written only after update-ca-certificates verifies. A retired root fails bundle and CApath verification after the next boot.

Tested scope: Hegel properties prove chunking-independent stamping and exact bounded retention. Rust unit cases cover the receiver's no-op, rotation, drift and failed-rebuild paths. Native boot-profile journeys on NixOS and Ubuntu boot through Lilly's real trust delivery with identical, added and retired root sets, verifying the guest bundle (and Ubuntu CApath links) after each boot.

- **property, recorded**: [stamping_is_chunking_independent](repo:lilly/native/boot-log/src/tests.rs) — Generated console bytes and chunkings stamp identically to the whole buffer and to an independent line oracle; prefix stripping recovers the input. Pure writer logic; no VMM or guest.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-10-guest-boot-profile.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [ubuntu_rotation_and_every_drift_take_the_full_path](repo:lyra/src/bin/overalls-trustd.rs) — Temporary-store receiver cases with an update-ca-certificates emulator: identical delivery is a no-op, rotation and five drift kinds rebuild, a failed rebuild withdraws the marker. Does not run the real Ubuntu tool.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-10-guest-boot-profile.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [a restart retiring that root removes it from the guest trust store](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/zfs-guest/boot-profile.py) — Real Firecracker NixOS and Ubuntu guests booted three times through Lilly trust delivery; boot report printed each boot; bundle membership after each delivery and Ubuntu CApath accept/refuse for present/retired roots. Nested KVM, isolated from Audi.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-10-guest-boot-profile.md).

**Gaps:** Nested-KVM 1-vCPU fixture timings only; no fleet-hardware measurement. ADR-0154's accepted at-most-30-second completion wait is unimplemented across in-flight tool timeouts; a controlled runner waited 40.25s, requiring a timeout-budget correction/regression. Isolated fixtures cannot finish booting without Audi, so systemd-analyze time is observed only on the NixOS image without private services. No curl verification against a platform-issued leaf certificate in this journey.

**Preferred test work:** Enforce the accepted completion-wait bound with a scoped timeout regression, record boot reports from fleet NixOS and Ubuntu creates after deployment, and add an issued-leaf TLS check to the rotation journey.

## Open a root or personal shell in a rebuilt guest and receive the stock Starship prompt

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, execution.

## Boot and restart a guest with the current host trust roots

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Current locally confined Firecracker boot, host-only vsock delivery, installed public trust and readiness ordering.

Required refusal: Reject a wrong-boot trust exchange without changing installed trust, service availability or durable receipt.

Tested scope: Strictly typed bounded NixOS/Ubuntu native fixture on two colocated Lilly nodes; exact host roots, actual guest services, local HTTP and retained data on restart. Wrong, forged and expired delivery mutations each terminate in completed peer-EOF refusals before unchanged receipt, installed bundle and service checks and a final accepted same-boot delivery. Sequential three-NixOS admission checks usable startup and durable ownership. A valid 17 GiB-root request exceeds the independently read actual 16 GiB quota; the fixture does not impose a settled virtual-promise cap or rerun the concurrent capacity race.

- **machine, recorded**: [every wrong, forged and expired boot trust mutation ends in a peer-EOF refusal with no response bytes](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/fleet-guest-trust/guest.exs) — Recorded on 40c1e73b (drv f62qs50m): six probe executions across both distributions; per probe, one wrong-boot exchange plus seven mutations of exactly one receiver check (protocol version, placement, stale execution epoch, nonce, forged digest claim, duplicated root, private-key-bearing PEM), with unchanged receipt, installed bundle and services verified after each sweep and a final accepted same-boot delivery. ## Reactivate a historical fleet snapshot safely

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Post-backup revocations, epochs, generations and physical survivors must be reconciled.

Required refusal: Never treat a readable restored database as current production authority.

Tested scope: Current-protection pins only: the isolated restore drill boots the release in operator mode against the restored database with no listener sockets and no background consumers; fixed Lilly tests pin monotonic command receipts under regressed replay, while generated terminal-error histories stop one to four actor processes and preserve durable placements without proving native guest survival; guest-facing identity checks reject journal-only authority after restore. No complete automated historical-fleet reactivation acceptance is identified; the quarantine-gate and default-deny design sketch (restore sentinel, fail-closed quarantine boot, reconcile report, gated finalization) remains proposal-only pending user delegation (candidate ADR-A quarantine gate, ADR-B default-deny re-enablement).

## Read the current host serial log while guest bootstrap or terminal capability is unavailable

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Marshall checks current Cedar VM read, unique current placement and fresh authenticated protocol-2 host stream independently of guest terminal capability. Lilly checks its assigned stream caller and newest runnable command, then binds a private single-link host log inode to unchanged boot, intent and launch-attempt evidence. Only a bounded page and cursor leave the host; no guest manager, dial, boot challenge, path or input authority is returned.

Required refusal: Refuse foreign or revoked readers, deleted VMs, stale or unsupported host streams, missing or ambiguous placement, superseded stop/delete/replacement commands, changed epoch/generation/incarnation, missing launch witness and unsafe files. An older same-epoch launch attempt permits only a still-running adopted execution with full confined-VMM observation; failed adopted logs remain unavailable. Guest terminal session creation/listing remains refused when capability is false.

Tested scope: Focused Lilly execution passed 55 checks (13 properties and 42 tests), including pending/failed current-command diagnostics, launch-witness and private-inode refusals, actor supersession and generated arbitrary-byte/cursor histories. Independent control-flow review found no remaining source blocker. The focused Marshall suite passed 27 tests covering synthetic native terminal-capability false, Cedar/freshness/protocol refusal, the direct Boot log link and diagnostic mode without guest listing or automatic opening. Structural Monospace, presentation JavaScript and Python static gates also passed. The final local browser fixture passed desktop/mobile, both themes, grid, contrast, origin-only resources and EOF/disconnect/reconnect/hide/destroy lifecycle. Complete Marshall and Lilly gates passed on clean589ff7fe5; later source changes retain their own checks. The diagnostic correction grants no guest terminal or native-image admission.

The native image row is seeded onto an ordinary fixture placement, not admitted or provisioned. No actual Lilly host, guest or browser.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-host-boot-log-authorization.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [boot-log reads still refuse foreign actors and stale or unsupported host streams](repo:marshall/test/marshall/terminal/authority_test.exs) — Foreign VM reader, old terminal protocol and stale host-report checks through the Marshall authority function; no real host stream or guest.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-host-boot-log-authorization.md).

## Enroll a replacement host with fresh physical identity after retiring the old one

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Deployment enrollment binds each host to its real machine identity, name and ZFS GUIDs. Retirement is the only way to release host authority permanently; the retired row is never recycled or renamed.

Required refusal: Refuse enrollment for recycled retired names, conflicting registrations and unready or unfresh hosts; refuse stale compute and inference credentials over every authenticated transport after retirement; refuse all issuance, sessions, exchanges, enablement and admission on a retired host forever.

Tested scope: Generated histories over the real Ash actions and authenticated control exchange against a pure model oracle, three-BEAM races for name and rotation serialization, and a native two-Lilly fleet journey with SOPS delivery, real v3 TLS sessions, real ZFS GUID binding and a nested guest reaching private services. Physical providers, production DNS/CA/load and multi-region are excluded.

- **unit, recorded**: [a resumed drain remains in history after a new drain request](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/enrollment_history_test.exs) — Real SQL-backed host history retains the closed drain alongside the current open request; focused file also reruns the two generated properties at the previously failing seed. No physical host replacement is exercised.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-27-host-replacement.md).
- **property, recorded**: [credential histories preserve live guest reservations byte for byte](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/enrollment_history_test.exs) — Rotation, revocation, admission toggles and maintenance on a host holding a real reservation; retirement refused while resources are held.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-27-host-replacement.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [retirement fences concurrent rotations into one terminal retired state](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/distributed_enrollment_test.exs) — Three independent BEAMs over one committed database: same-name convergence/conflict, host-lock rotation serialization with idempotent prepared retries, and retirement fencing rotations in either lock order; seeded lock/fence mutants fire elsewhere in the suite inventory.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-09-27-host-replacement.md).

## Hold every Lilly lease and leased utility in lilly-hostd until the holder releases it or dies

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: lilly-hostd holds each lease's flock on the existing lock inode, grants waiters in arrival order and runs leased utilities from a closed table with the lease descriptor inherited, each in its own command cgroup in production.

Required refusal: No successor lease while a utility of the previous holder may run; no mutating utility without a lease; no second command on a busy lease; no session for a wrong uid, cgroup or protocol version.

Tested scope: hostd library tests (decoder and lease-order Hegel properties, real-utility session custody) and Lilly lock tests against the real daemon. Unit tests use process-group custody; cgroup custody is exercised only by module-based NixOS machine tests.

- **property, recorded**: [lease_grants_follow_arrival_order](repo:lilly/native/hostd/src/tests.rs) — Generated exclusive and shared waiter sequences behind a held lease; grant order and mutual exclusion replayed against an independent model.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-16-lilly-hostd-core.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [holder-death-kills-leased-command](repo:lilly/test/host/lock_test.exs) — A holder killed with a cp blocked on a FIFO under its lease; the successor is granted only after hostd killed the utility.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-16-lilly-hostd-core.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [completed native launch survives abrupt worker BEAM loss and fresh Store reopen](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/zfs-guest/actor-recovery.py) — Real guests created, read and deleted through the production lilly-hostd unit with cgroup custody, including abrupt worker BEAM loss.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-16-lilly-hostd-core.md).

**Gaps:** Arguments remain caller-supplied until typed native effects replace the utility table. The peer cgroup check reads /proc after connect rather than through a pidfd. Lilly and hostd both run as root until the privilege drop.

**Preferred test work:** A dedicated host-effects-custody machine test for wrong-peer refusal, BEAM SIGKILL mid-command and escaped descendants under cgroup custody.

## Reach Firecracker jail sockets and guest ingress from the unprivileged Lilly BEAM without leaking descriptors

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: The BEAM holds only sockets it created (ADR-0184). lilly-hostd connects Lilly's own socket to api.sock or v.sock beneath pool roots, or, as a fallback only, bridges it to a namespace connection through lilly-ingress-bridge running as lilly (op 13); every ingress service instead sends Audi's accepted connection to a detached bridge (ADR-0187, ADR-0192). hostd sends no descriptor and Lilly closes each socket after its gen_tcp port is down.

Required refusal: hostd refuses a received descriptor that is not an unconnected, non-listening AF_UNIX stream socket and paths outside its socket roots, and ends the session on a descriptor with any other request, a missing descriptor or more than one.

Tested scope: hostd fixture tests and Hegel decoding models, bridge process fixtures (privilege drop under sudo), and a Lilly custody property test with a negative control. No VM namespace or Firecracker process.

- **property, recorded**: [adopted sockets are released exactly when their port goes down](repo:lilly/test/host/sockets_custody_test.exs) — Random close, owner-death and controlling_process transfers over sockets the BEAM connected itself in place of hostd; peers see end of stream and the descriptor count returns to baseline.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-lilly-owns-every-socket.md).
- **property, recorded**: [connect_unix_decoding_matches_model](repo:lilly/native/hostd/src/descriptor_tests.rs) — Ops 12 and 13 decode against independent models; fixture daemons connect, refuse and end sessions over real Unix sockets.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-lilly-owns-every-socket.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [unprivileged Lilly releases every socket it uses](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/fleet/scenarios/socket-custody.py) — Lilly's socket descriptor count on both provisioners over a minute with guests running.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-lilly-owns-every-socket.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [Overalls CLI opens an interactive Firecracker Bash shell with Starship and its home](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/fleet/scenarios/user-ssh-journey.py) — Guest SSH from the Overalls CLI through Audi and Lilly's ingress socket, which the unprivileged BEAM can only reach through hostd op 13 and lilly-ingress-bridge; key revocation, relocation, reboot and cloning in the same run.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-lilly-owns-every-socket.md).

**Gaps:** Fleet and user-SSH journey runs on df94ad026/b55b4e1ad record the namespace dial, guest SSH through lilly-ingress-bridge and the flat descriptor count. Op 13 bridges, now only a fallback, still end on a hostd or Lilly restart; guest SSH survival is the detached-ingress-bridge-survival scenario and editor/nested HTTPS survival the staged-detached-ingress-survival scenario.

## Pin a machine to the top of the lists and keep it from being deleted until the owner unpins it

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: A pin is a per-user Access row with a two-state machine (pinned, unpinned) and one live row per user/machine; it confers no authority. The lifecycle coordinator reads the owner's live pinned row under the VM lock and refuses every delete path with machine_pinned; the owner's account deletion archives the owner's pins first; both VM archive sites archive every remaining pin.

Required refusal: Refuse pinning without current read access, on deleted intent (vm_deleted) and past twenty pins (pin_limit); refuse browser, Fleet workloads, SSH/Porsche rm and thread deletes while the owner holds a pin; never let a shared user's pin fence deletion or a pin extend revoked access.

Tested scope: Generated owner/member pin and delete histories through the real domain action and the real SSH rm path against local PostgreSQL, a per-user ordered-set model over three machines, pagination with random page sizes, LiveView toggles on the list, overview and header with the disabled Delete and refusal flash, SSH pin/unpin/rm command tests and the cross-application closed reason set. No native journey.

## A Linux user adds a deployment, approves Mila in the browser, sees their machines and follows overalls:// links, and still sees the saved list after a restart

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, storage.

Boundary: The Linux bundle reaches the deployment only through the pinned trust document and Porsche SSH; approval happens in the authenticated production web page after fingerprint comparison; links only navigate; settings, device keys and snapshots are owner-only.

Required refusal: An unknown deployment's link lands on the deployment list, a second invocation never opens a second window, snapshots hold no approval links or tokens, and a saved list's actions are disabled.

Tested scope: NixOS machine test with real X input, packaged Marshall, haproxy and Porsche, and Playwright Chromium for the approval. Machines are not provisioned (no Lilly), so the live list is empty.

**Preferred test work:** Run the same journey in a fleet fixture with a provisioned machine.

## Mila connects to a deployment only after verifying its Porsche host certificate against the pinned trust document

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, transport, recovery.

Boundary: Mila fetches https://HOST/bin/ssh-trust.json without redirects, pins it, and in key exchange accepts only an Ed25519 host certificate from the pinned CA naming the management host inside its validity window, before user authentication.

Required refusal: Another CA, another principal, an expired certificate or a plain host key ends the connection before the device key signs; a conflicting later trust document is refused and the pin kept; an unreachable origin uses only an unretired pin.

Tested scope: Dart certificate verification against Elixir-issued fixtures, trust resolution, and five journeys against a stock OpenSSH server in the Nix sandbox; mutation-checked by disabling the host check.

- **unit, recorded**: [LiveSession](repo:mila/native/linux/src/session.rs) — Stock OpenSSH server presenting host certificates in the mila-transport Nix check.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-mila-m1.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [LiveSession](repo:mila/native/linux/src/session.rs) — Trust document pinning and reconciliation.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-mila-m1.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [LiveSession](repo:mila/native/linux/src/session.rs) — Elixir-issued certificate fixtures get the same verdict in Dart.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-mila-m1.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [LiveSession](repo:mila/native/linux/src/session.rs) — Real Porsche release refusing a rogue CA without an authentication record; Marshall is absent, so commands end in an authority envelope.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-mila-m1.md).

**Gaps:** The real-Porsche fixture has no Marshall, so a full signed-in command journey through Porsche to Marshall is not yet exercised from Mila.

**Preferred test work:** Extend the mila-desktop NixOS machine test to a signed-in journey through Porsche and Marshall.

## Restart the same native disk under fresh authority after an observed abrupt VMM process failure

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: The fixture flushes and reads back exact home bytes, requires actual Firecracker SIGKILL, then boots the same disk with fresh MMDS authority. Native filesystem verification and retained bytes are required after recovery; final shutdown must be observed cleanly.

Required refusal: Refuse old flush, workspace and terminal authority after restart. Refuse incomplete filesystem checks, corrupt or missing retained bytes, an unobserved SIGKILL, reused boot identity or unclean final exit; incomplete histories cannot publish a receipt.

Tested scope: Seven host boundary checks and the composed NixOS driver passed. An initial FreeBSD crash run exposed scheduled-only libc sync and lost acknowledged home/marker bytes. The corrected native UFS suspension/resume flush passed the final reviewed image 5022d714 crash variant in 224 seconds: observed SIGKILL, same-disk/new-MMDS/new-boot restart, exact retained bytes, stale-authority refusal, native UFS snapshot background fsck, all eight crash checks, both complete service oracles and final clean exit. The source-qualified OmniOS image then passed the crash variant with image SHA-256 d47a84fd726276865bea26812c2a3624b88144eda87926e2dd6dbd5dccb98bc8, kernel c56dc5c19523ef29511e2bfe4b98a6544b786a089b55b654c30ea32e821bdd21, firmware 261c6d43a4d74e6e7f4ea98390b35b6e0d90c511cf961e4b7abb60410b1c24a2 and VMM ba91e85a7af3f96d02f845df543daec07353ed6bff4aaee0abf524c751476b68. Its immutable crash receipt records SIGKILL, fresh MMDS/boot identity, stale-authority refusal, exact retained bytes, completed zero-error ZFS scrub and clean shutdown; both image families retain native_admission=false. Final unchanged OmniOS 45983 disk separately passed the same-disk process-SIGKILL runner with endings sigkill,clean, fresh authority/boot identity, exact retained bytes and native ZFS integrity checks.

Its full matrix and separate publication/source activation do not establish physical host recovery or a Marshall-owned fleet journey.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-github-com-integration.md).

Separate isolation failure leaves full matrix qualification and admission incomplete.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-github-com-integration.md).
