## Stop an executing native guest command when its current executor lease or supervisor authority is withdrawn

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: Marshall owns executor fences and transitions; the guest uses only verified private HTTPS. Native exec_command forwards the existing lease/stop callback before spawn and during authority polling. A separate scoped collector owns the child, concurrently bounds both output streams and enforces the 20-second deadline independently of a blocking lease RPC.

Required refusal: A refused pre-spawn callback must create no child. Running refusal must cancel the separate process group, reap the direct child and discard output; execute must not publish a result under the failed lease. Missing/failed private authority and supervisor stop fail closed without logging command bytes.

Tested scope: The production native callback wiring and scoped cancellation/deadline collector are implemented. All six local real-process command tests passed, including no-spawn refusal, running cancellation/reaping/output suppression and a blocked lease RPC. Historical source-qualified OmniOS service evidence is retained. Fresh FreeBSD image 0150b6d1 passed all five exact-artifact scenarios against current VMM f0d9275b with executor withdrawal/cancellation and fresh-fence completion on every boot. Exact OmniOS 679f5f8b passed current-VMM services, growth, crash and daemon recovery with the same executor boundary on each complete service boot. Its isolation boot 0 reached those checks before shutdown-send failed; that incomplete scenario adds no complete receipt. Old-VMM results retain their separate scope.

- **machine, recorded**: [executor-whole-group-death-no-result-and-fresh-fence-completion](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/native-services/driver.py) — Current-VMM FreeBSD 0150b6d1 passed all five unchanged scenarios with executor withdrawal/cancellation and fresh-fence completion on every boot. Synthetic authority and exact immutable native artifacts; no live Marshall revocation or physical host isolation guarantee.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-github-com-integration.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [executor-whole-group-death-no-result-and-fresh-fence-completion](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/native-services/driver.py) — Current-VMM OmniOS 679f5f8b passed services, growth, crash and daemon recovery with the executor checks on every complete service boot. Isolation failed after boot 0's executor checks at shutdown-send and produced no complete scenario receipt. No admission, live control-plane revocation or physical host isolation guarantee.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-github-com-integration.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [fn refused_authority_never_spawns_a_command()](repo:lyra/src/agent/native_command.rs) — Local real-process fixture refuses before a marker-producing shell can start; no native guest or control-plane lease.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-native-image-admission.md).

Isolated synthetic private authority; no Marshall fleet or live GitHub claim.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-github-com-integration.md).

## Refuse stale guest attribution while retaining genuine native exit evidence

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: Volatile proof binds the exact currently verified VMM; one native observer may outlive proof withdrawal to report its actual terminal outcome, without granting authority.

Required refusal: Negative evidence immediately withdraws proof; unavailable or unarmed targets retain the short backstop, stale ports cannot renew it, and a different boot target cannot inherit live authority.

Tested scope: Deterministic real-port ordering regressions, generated watch-machine terminal transitions and the final typed native Brady VMM-kill/attribution-refusal journey pass. Actual exact-target watcher revocation took 99 milliseconds under the original less-than-1000-millisecond bound.

- **unit, recorded**: [an observation before watcher exit withdraws proof but retains the actual report](repo:lilly/test/vm/actor_watch_test.exs) — Controlled physical observation precedes the existing real port's actual terminal output; immediate proof withdrawal, unchanged retained port, no renewal from late armed and exactly one genuine exited event pass. Error, target replacement, unavailable binding, boot-only replacement, stale-port and shutdown cases pass separately. No native pidfd or physical isolation claim.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-09-observability-decoupling.md).
- **property, recorded**: [terminal reports always revoke and only :absent opens a watcher](repo:lilly/test/vm/actor_watch_test.exs) — Generated watcher-machine terminal transitions require revocation and bounded open effects. This property does not generate actor proof-target or journal/port ordering histories and does not establish native process behavior.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-09-observability-decoupling.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [brady-vmm-death-revokes-via-watcher](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/fleet/scenarios/brady.py) — Real target VMM SIGKILL with one bound watcher and matching pidfd; actual exact-placement exited witness, 99-millisecond revocation under the original subsecond requirement and unresolved old-flow attribution. Complete typed Brady native script passed in 359.64 seconds on the captured pre-Starship guest runtime; no physical host failure claim.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-09-observability-decoupling.md).

**Gaps:** Generated cross-target observation/arming histories remain absent. Native acceptance uses the captured guest runtime before incoming Starship defaults; physical host failure remains separate.

**Preferred test work:** Generate cross-target event histories with journal contention and delayed native callbacks; deterministic ordering is used to reproduce the specific race reliably. Validate physical host loss separately.

## Keep a native guest's acknowledged bytes and root consistent across interrupted growth, host power loss and relocation to another host

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Real FreeBSD and OmniOS images boot in nested KVM with Lilly's Writeback/Sync drive mode on a disk file inside a host ZFS dataset and fresh MMDS placement, epoch and boot challenge. Interrupted growth SIGKILLs the VMM at traced writes past the old disk end; power loss replays only the dm-log-writes journal prefix before the cut; relocation moves a stopped disk by ZFS send/receive to a second host and boots it under a new placement.

Required refusal: Refuse a FreeBSD flush receipt unless a device cache flush succeeds. Fail on an inconsistent filesystem, a root size other than old or new, a surviving unflushed host canary, missing or altered acknowledged bytes, a mismatched snapshot GUID or workspace digest, reused boot identity, or acceptance of flush, workspace or terminal authority from the pre-cut boot or source placement.

Tested scope: All six ADR-0243 checks passed on final source. A pre-fix FreeBSD candidate lost its acknowledged marker after power-cut replay because UFS sends no BIO_FLUSH; the agent now issues DIOCGFLUSH and the rebuilt candidate passed with 36 device flushes inside the guest-flush segment. Promoted OmniOS omniosGuest passed growth (430.14 s), power loss (267.22 s) and relocation (300.46 s); the FreeBSD candidate passed growth (307.38 s), power loss (192.05 s) and relocation (206.07 s). Receipts retain native_admission=false.

- **machine, recorded**: [Power loss MUST place the host pool on dm-log-writes](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/native-durability/default.nix) — The pre-fix FreeBSD candidate failed with fsck exit 0 but a missing acknowledged marker. After the DIOCGFLUSH fix FreeBSD passed in 192.05 s and promoted OmniOS in 267.22 s: host canary lost, exact marker bytes, new epoch/challenge/boot identity, pre-cut authority refused and clean shutdown.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [Relocation MUST move a stopped guest between two hosts by](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/native-durability/default.nix) — FreeBSD (206.07 s) and OmniOS (300.46 s) moved a stopped disk by ZFS send/receive, matched snapshot GUIDs and the workspace SHA-256 on the destination, booted under a new placement and refused source-placement flush, workspace and terminal authority. No Lilly or Marshall orchestration.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).

## Fence native socket identity and wake blocked operations after an actual Firecracker transport event

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, recovery.

## Open a public provider link, sign in, or run overalls open to create an OSS machine with a guest-owned checkout

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Public CSRF capture grants no authority and stores only canonical source2, visit and expiry in the signed cookie. A current ordinary stored login or registered-key Porsche identity admits through Compute and a matching manifest4 source capability; ordinary browser provisioning requires no passkey. The postcommit receipt rechecks login and VM ownership before matched clear. Lilly carries inert source2 bound to current placement, epoch and boot; only the guest contacts providers and runs git. Existing immutable snapshots/receiver records are never rewritten during cutover. Every validated new provision/start snapshot derives source from the durable VM, including supplied resize snapshots. Recovery preflights durable image eligibility without discarding valid crash/resize proof or fresh host reports.

Required refusal: Source queries/fragments never enter capture storage/POST; URL user information refuses there, and raw authority/path stays strict backend input. Malformed or expired capture, missing CSRF, revoked or MFA-pending identity creates no machine. Unsupported origins/routes, option-shaped values, non-egress profiles, absent/obsolete/mismatched source capability and changed source under one idempotency key refuse before allocation. A stale completion cannot clear a newer observed capture. Stale boots, source conflicts, foreign API clone origins, redirects and obsolete stored sources refuse; a done marker cannot bypass stored-source validation. Supplied snapshots cannot replace the retained immutable image or recorded source. Unavailable restart capability releases only confirmed stopped compute and retains disk/address; confirmed resize completes a fixed source-unavailable failure, preserving target sizes and ordinary cleanup.

Tested scope: Incoming browser-feature source2 grammar/manifest properties, SQL-backed capture/MFA/dedupe/admission histories, initial Lilly driver refusal, boot delivery/journal properties and Rust receiver/CLI tests retain their captured scope before ADR0158 integration. ## Observe healthy pool capacity beside an exactly owned retained disk with invalid launch metadata

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: A pool-locked native allocation audit independently binds durable claim/spec, host/pool/VM nonce, GUID, mounts, closed file set, drive UID/type/length and ready-disk metadata. A safely contained private single-link marker is bounded to 16 KiB; boot artifacts must be nonempty root-owned single-link regular files with mode 0444 and combined marker/artifact sizes within the protocol's 1 GiB reservation. Only then may invalid bundle contents leave that child recognized without allocation credit, without decoding those contents. Measured ZFS free space still includes its bytes and any outstanding startup hold remains unoffset. Current launch/readiness codecs, authenticated capacity reports, startup settlement, cleanup authority and ADR-0159's no-legacy policy remain unchanged.

Required refusal: Unknown children, foreign or corrupt claims/owners/GUIDs, unsafe mounts/drives/boot-file custody, damaged disk metadata, exceeded artifact bounds and unexpected files continue to withhold the pool. An invalid launch bundle cannot grant allocation credit, readiness, execution, image admission, metadata conversion or deletion authority. Recognition of retained storage cannot authorize guest access or physical cleanup.

Tested scope: The focused NixOS machine fixture passed in 221.51 seconds, exit 0. It prepares two real owned disks on mirrored ZFS, substitutes unsupported boot-bundle version 999 on one, and requires repeated fresh-process no-credit and readiness refusals while its valid neighbor retains credit and marker SHA-256 remains unchanged. Corrupt disk metadata, unsafe kernel permissions, a foreign nonce and an unexpected file withhold the pool; restoring the original marker restores both credits before normal fixture cleanup. Exact derivation and scope are in the capacity review.

- **machine, recorded**: [invalid launch metadata preserves owned capacity without allocation credit](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/zfs-lifecycle/retained-bundle.py) — Passed 221.51-second disposable native ZFS ownership, no-credit, valid-neighbor, readiness refusal, unchanged bytes, independent corruption refusals, restoration and fixture cleanup; no guest boot or production mutation.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-retained-bundle-capacity.md).

**Gaps:** No guest boot, live deployment, production retained-data purge, concurrent bundle replacement, generated malformed-bundle histories, process-crash or physical power-loss result is established. This native storage case does not prove guest/host isolation, fleet admission or workload availability.

**Preferred test work:** Extend the recorded focused native fixture with generated ownership and malformed-bundle histories across fresh audit processes. Preserve strict launch/readiness and independent storage refusals; a host unit test cannot establish native ZFS behavior.

## An identity provider provisions, deactivates, deletes and reactivates Marshall users over SCIM, and users sign in with single sign-on

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Only the current SCIM bearer token (digest-compared) reaches /scim/v2. Deactivation or DELETE revokes logins at once, pauses owned machines and schedules deletion after the shared seven-day grace; reactivation inside grace resumes only SCIM-paused machines; after the deadline machines are deleted and the identity is ghosted and cannot be resurrected. While SCIM is enabled magic-link sign-in is refused and OIDC sign-in requires a JWKS-verified ID token whose sub matches an active SCIM externalId.

Required refusal: Wrong, empty or Basic credentials get 401; forged, unsigned, re-signed, wrong-audience, wrong-issuer, expired or nonce-less ID tokens and replayed or state-mismatched flows are refused; inactive identities are refused by logins, SSH key sessions, agents and admission; reactivation after the deadline and writes to finalized identities are refused.

Tested scope: BEAM endpoint, Oban and Hegel histories against PostgreSQL plus a NixOS machine test of the deployed TLS endpoint; see ADR-0229.

- **machine, recorded**: [Deactivation starts the seven-day retirement and deletion hides the account](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/scim/default.nix) — Packaged Marshall in a NixOS VM: authenticated SCIM user create, PATCH active=false, DELETE and GET 404 over TLS with a read-only probe of the retirement deadline; deadline expiry is not exercised.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).
- **property, recorded**: [SCIM event histories never delete early and never resurrect](repo:marshall/test/marshall/scim/lifecycle_property_test.exs) — Generated deactivate/reactivate/delete/clock/worker histories against the real resources and Oban worker in the BEAM test VM.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).
- **property, recorded**: [replacing any character of a signed ID token is always rejected](repo:marshall/test/marshall/scim/oidc_id_token_property_test.exs) — Generated tampering, truncation and algorithm substitution of RS256/ES256 ID tokens against the production verifier.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [machines pause at deactivation and are deleted only after the deadline](repo:marshall/test/marshall/scim/user_lifecycle_oban_test.exs) — Oban worker with the deadline moved into the past, against PostgreSQL; no native machine reclamation.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [query-supplied identity claims without a code never sign in](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/scim_oidc_controller_test.exs) — Controller flow against a fake identity provider; no real provider or browser.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).

**Gaps:** The machine test does not advance past the seven-day deadline, so deadline deletion and finalization are BEAM-only; no browser OIDC journey runs natively; the OIDC client secret is stored in plaintext.

**Preferred test work:** Add a machine test that shortens the configured grace period and observes native machine deletion and finalization, and a browser OIDC journey against a fake provider.

## An identity provider manages Marshall teams through SCIM Groups while people view their teams and all teams read-only

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: SCIM Groups create, rename, update membership and delete SCIM-managed teams owned only by the hidden service owner. While SCIM is enabled no native team can be created and native membership, invitation and ownership transfer are refused; SCIM-managed teams stay locked after SCIM is disabled. Enabling SCIM retires native teams: after the grace deadline their authority is revoked, machines are deleted through Compute and the team is archived.

Required refusal: Native team mutations, transfers and new team resources on retiring or SCIM-managed teams are refused over the web and SSH; unauthenticated or disabled SCIM Group requests are refused; the service owner cannot be removed or changed.

Tested scope: BEAM HTTP, Oban, LiveView and Hegel membership histories against PostgreSQL plus a NixOS machine test of Group provisioning and native-team retirement scheduling; see ADR-0229 and ADR-0077.

- **property, recorded**: [SCIM membership converges to the model with exactly one hidden owner](repo:marshall/test/marshall/scim/team_scim_property_test.exs) — Generated create/add/remove/replace/rename/delete Group histories through the real endpoint against PostgreSQL.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-20-scim-completion.md).

## Keep a live browser editor WebSocket or nested HTTPS connection through lilly-hostd and Lilly restarts while Lilly still decides its preface, readiness and lifetime

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: authorization, transport, execution, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: ADR-0192. Editor and nested HTTPS take ADR-0187's detached path (record, op 14, keeper, re-adoption, ending through hostd). Lilly derives the stage from the validated binding: a PROXY v2 header naming the Audi-attested client for nested HTTPS, the framed editor binding and the exact framed ready document for the editor. hostd writes the preface to the guest and byte-compares exactly the expected frame's length, reading no guest byte past it, before starting the bridge; it interprets neither string. TLS, HTTP and per-request editor grants stay with the client, the nested guest, Audi and Marshall.

Required refusal: hostd refuses an op 14 whose preface exceeds 4096 bytes, whose expected frame exceeds 256 bytes or whose ready wait is not 0 without a frame and 1..30000 ms with one, and starts no bridge when the guest closes, stays silent past the wait or sends any other frame. Editor sign-out still closes the WebSocket at Audi, which ends the bridge; a restarted Lilly ends unrecorded bridges and recorded ones whose execution is not current within 30 s. Marshall answers editor and web renewal while Lilly reconnects with unavailable, which Audi retries only inside the unchanged lease; sign-out, revoked write, stop, a newer generation and a stale report stay conclusive refusals.

Tested scope: hostd Hegel op 14 decoding model and the stage test over socket pairs; Lilly connector tests with a fake host for editor and nested HTTPS handoff, records and the derived stage. Marshall editor and web renewal across a simulated Lilly reconnect and conclusive revocations; Audi renewal against a scripted control channel. The editor fleet restart subtest's first run failed on Marshall's renewal refusal; the corrected subtest has not run. No nested HTTPS machine evidence (Inception is out of scope).

- **property, recorded**: [ingress_decoding_matches_model](repo:lilly/native/hostd/src/ingress_tests.rs) — op 14 with greeting, preface, expected frame and ready wait against an independent decoding model, and the stage over socket pairs: whole preface written, exact frame accepted, later bytes left unread, a different frame, a closed guest and a silent guest refused.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [editor and nested HTTPS connections are bridged detached and recorded](repo:lilly/test/ingress_bridges_test.exs) — Editor and nested HTTPS bindings take the detached path against a fake host, are recorded with the nested client endpoint and guarded; the derived stage is empty for SSH, one PROXY v2 header for nested HTTPS and the editor binding with the exact ready frame for the editor.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [renewal across a Lilly restart is inconclusive while reconnecting, then keeps the binding](repo:marshall/test/marshall/editor_test.exs) — Real editor domain authority: after a host disconnect and a new unreported session, renewal is temporarily_unavailable and admission is refused; after the first report renewal keeps the exact binding. A stale report, sign-out and a stop with a newer generation stay conclusive while reconnecting. The web equivalent is in ingress/access_test.exs.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [an unavailable renewal during a Lilly restart is retried and the stream survives](repo:audi/test/http_authority_test.exs) — A scripted control channel answers unavailable twice and then the unchanged grant; the stream owner outlives its original deadline. unauthorized, forbidden and authentication_required end it at that renewal, before the deadline.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-17-staged-detached-ingress.md).
- **machine, present**: [live editor WebSockets survive lilly-hostd and Lilly restarts in detached bridges](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/vscode-web/fleet.py) — With a live browser editor, restart lilly-hostd and then Lilly, each past the 30 s adoption grace: bridges holding the guest's port 4444 sit in lilly_ingress.slice scopes and survive, every editor WebSocket stays open and receives frames afterwards, and a fresh editor request succeeds. Present; its first run failed on Marshall's renewal refusal, and the corrected subtest has not run..

**Gaps:** The editor fleet restart subtest's first run failed because Marshall pinned the editor lease to Lilly's replaced control session and refused renewal while Lilly reconnected; the corrected subtest has not run. Nested HTTPS has unit and property evidence only, and its renewal still pins the host session through its publication, so a nested HTTPS stream survives a hostd restart but not a Lilly restart. Nested porsche_ssh and audi_ssh renewal has the same publication binding. hostd, a root process, reads up to 256 guest bytes for the editor's ready frame; moving the stage into the unprivileged bridge is an open question. A detached editor's scope start now follows the guest's ready frame inside Audi's unchanged 22 s handshake bound.

**Preferred test work:** Record a passing vscode-web-nixos-fleet run of the editor restart subtest; nested HTTPS waits on a working Inception fleet.

## Deliver a Mila notification through Susan without revealing content

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, storage.

Boundary: Only a push key Susan can open plus a valid install signature admits a poke; providers receive only ciphertext, collapse id and fixed loc-keys.

Required refusal: Forged signatures, unknown/denied keys and malformed bodies answer the same 404/400 body and write nothing.

Tested scope: Packaged release, real SOPS bundle, local PostgreSQL and verify_peer TLS to local fake APNs/OAuth/FCM origins.

- **machine, recorded**: [APNs poke is content-free and over HTTP/2 with verified TLS](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/susan-service/driver.py) — Fake provider origins behind a private CA.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-19-mila-m6.md).
- **property, present**: [arbitrary event sequences never send before every check and always answer once](repo:susan/test/susan/machine_property_test.exs) — Pure FSM..

**Gaps:** No real Apple or Google acceptance; hosting and TLS placement open.

**Preferred test work:** Exercise sandbox APNs and FCM with publisher credentials once hosting is chosen.

## Retry a poke without double notification and bound abuse

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: execution, recovery.

Boundary: A sent delivery id is answered 204 without a second send; per-key, install, source and global token buckets bound throughput.

Required refusal: Replays answer 400; the eleventh burst poke answers 429 with Retry-After; deny-listed keys answer 404; unregistered tokens answer 410 and stay cached.

Tested scope: susan-service machine test and Hegel token-bucket/replay properties.

- **machine, recorded**: [provider 503 retries once in-request, then a later retry succeeds once](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/susan-service/driver.py) — Single node.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-19-mila-m6.md).
- **property, present**: [admissions never exceed burst plus refill and refusals name a sufficient wait](repo:susan/test/susan/token_bucket_property_test.exs) — Pure arithmetic..

**Gaps:** Buckets are per node; multi-instance limits are untested.

**Preferred test work:** Machine test with two Susan nodes behind one proxy.

## Operate Susan's secrets and audit trail

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: storage, recovery, identity.

Boundary: Secrets arrive only through the host-bound SOPS bundle and systemd credentials; the audit trail is append-only and hash chained.

Required refusal: Another host cannot decrypt the bundle; a missing secret keeps the previous bundle and fences startup; unsafe credential files and invalid keyrings refuse startup; UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on audit rows fail.

Tested scope: susan-secrets and susan-service machine tests; susan-image for the container form.

- **machine, recorded**: [keyring rotation is audited and older push keys still open](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/susan-secrets/driver.py) — Single host plus a wrong-host node.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-19-mila-m6.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [no secret bytes in image layers or the container filesystem](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/susan-image/driver.py) — Rootful podman.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-19-mila-m6.md).

**Gaps:** secrets/overalls-susan.enc.json holds placeholder values only, encrypted to the recovery recipients and the salopettes host (ADR-0231); real APNs/FCM credentials are not installed.

**Preferred test work:** Replace the placeholders with real provider credentials and repeat susan-secrets against the salopettes document.

## A Windows Mila exchanges its WNS channel URI for a push key and later receives a raw poke

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: transport, authorization.

Boundary: Susan admits a WNS channel URI only in the susan-wns-channel-shape form, seals it in the push key and re-checks it before each send; Entra ID tokens come from the compiled login.microsoftonline.com origin.

Required refusal: A channel URI with another scheme, host, port, userinfo, fragment or length, or a sandbox environment, is refused with the fixed 400; WNS 404/410 marks the token unregistered and 401 refreshes the Entra token once.

Tested scope: BEAM unit and Hegel property tests over the fake provider transport. The Nix service module does not enable WNS and no machine test fakes a WNS origin.

- **property, present**: [an accepted channel always posts to a notify.windows.com host on 443](repo:susan/test/susan/wns_channel_property_test.exs) — Hegel over schemes, host suffixes, ports, userinfo and paths..
- **unit, present**: [a WNS key sends a raw notification to its channel after one Entra exchange](repo:susan/test/susan/poke_test.exs) — Poke pipeline over Susan.FakeProvider..

**Gaps:** WNS is not enabled in the deployed Susan, no Entra credentials exist, and Susan's config-loading tests run only on Linux.

**Preferred test work:** Extend the susan-service machine test with WNS credentials and a fake *.notify.windows.com origin behind its private CA once the service module gains wnsAppIds.

Tested scope: A Hegel state-machine property against PostgreSQL, graph and accepted-attribute units, PostgreSQL-backed server-tool units for Cedar-visible search and claim-time access refusal, and one present but unrecorded NixOS machine test.

- **unit, present**: [no thread action accepts the status attribute](repo:marshall/test/marshall/threads/thread_state_machine_property_test.exs) — Static check of every Thread action's accepted attributes and the declared transition graph..

- **unit, present**: [revoked machine access cancels the command before it runs](repo:marshall/test/marshall/agents/server_tool_test.exs) — Claim-time Access recheck and closed refusal reason; no effect beyond the command and its audit rows..

Focused run passed on 2026-10-21..

## Retain host mutation or transfer custody until every adopted utility child retires

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Native helpers retain completion custody (the source-export lock; the transfer-stream hostd lease) across descendant process groups/sessions; direct leader exit does not prove cleanup.

Required refusal: Do not reply success/failure, admit successor mutation or release custody while independently observed adopted children remain live.

Tested scope: Native3library/9integration checks passed138s, rustfmt/Clippy; completion and early producer/EOF selector mutants caught. Actual native processes, inherited descriptors, independent flock contenders and complete PID retirement; not physical storage or VM isolation.

- **property, recorded**: [escaped_stream_failure_retains_custody_until_actual_reaping](repo:lilly/native/transfer-stream/tests/stream.rs) — The helper as lilly-hostd runs it (ADR-0183): no lock or stdin channel, completion custody until every adopted child is reaped. Local run of the hosted CLI only; no physical ZFS/SSH, cgroup confinement or hosted claim.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-16-guest-dataset-streams-in-hostd.md).

**Gaps:** Owned source/tests match the passing archived native input after integration. Exact-helper Lilly precommit passed506checks and forced test Dialyzer with zero errors/skips; evaluated publication and other consumers remain open. Escaped children may require explicit death; blocking all-child wait does not establish bounded cgroup containment, uninterruptible-I/O recovery, physical ZFS/SSH or hosted faults. Mutant credit ends at the first witnessed failure.

**Preferred test work:** Run full Lilly using the exact verified helper binaries and then native storage/host lifecycle composition.

## Send Underclass provider traffic, and only that traffic, out through the operator's Australian tailnet exit node

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, transport, isolation, recovery.

Boundary: Dedicated unprivileged userspace tailnet node per host with its own state and socket; Underclass cgroup limited to loopback behind a privileged exit-node start gate; host tailscaled, routes and other services unchanged.

## Receive a served response instead of “Selected model is at capacity” when one pool account's upstream stream overloads before output

Coverage: **gap**. Layers: authorization, recovery.

Boundary: The pinned Underclass proxy holds a streamed 2xx response, for at most 60 seconds or 1 MiB, until its first output or terminal event. It retries on another pool account only when that terminal event is a capacity failure with no output before it, and it never sends a byte to the client from a discarded attempt. The overloaded account keeps its health and is skipped only for that request.

Required refusal: Policy, quota and other failure codes are never retried on another account, and an error after any output passes through unchanged. When every account overloads, the client receives the original upstream bytes rather than a synthesized error, no banked reset is redeemed, and the SLO journal records one failure for the request.

Tested scope: Upstream dbaf7b8 cargo unit, Hegel property and end-to-end tests passed on the source with the fleet instrumentation patch and slo.rs applied, including failover, every-account-overloaded replay and overload-after-output pass-through cases; the fleet package built offline. NixOS checks were not run on this pin.



**Gaps:** No NixOS test drives an overloading upstream through the instrumented service, so SLO outcome counting across a failover is verified only by source review; live provider overload behavior on this revision is unobserved.

**Preferred test work:** Extend the Underclass NixOS service test with an upstream fixture that overloads one account before output; verify the client receives the other account's response, the SLO journal records one success, and an all-accounts overload records one failure.

## Choose a display time zone in the profile section of the account page, read every timestamp in that zone and see collaborators' local time

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: The zone is a nullable display preference on the user's own row, written only through the self-only set_time_zone action and validated against the compiled tz database; storage, ledger time, CSV export and SSH wire views stay UTC. The viewer zone resolves saved, then validated browser connect param, then UTC; other people's local time renders only from a saved zone.

Required refusal: Refuse unknown or malformed zones with invalid_time_zone, non-user actors with Forbidden and retired accounts with unauthorized; required/security minute ticks first refuse revoked or expired persisted logins. Never persist the browser zone, log the zone text, show a person's local time without a saved zone, or add browser-only fields to SSH ls/show, share show or team show.

Tested scope: Hegel properties over every curated zone and random instants including DST edges for label offsets, ordering, uniqueness, antisymmetric differences and validation; database round trips of the action; LiveView tests of the profile page, resolution order, dead render, UTC-provenance timestamps and people on team, machine, thread and Control room pages; Covenant obligations; synthetic browser probe of the profile page and an Adelaide timestamp. During integration through 9e7f6bd3, 49 focused tests passed, including actual persisted-token revocation refused on the next clock tick after correcting hook order. No native journey.

- **property, present**: [every label carries the zone's offset in force at that instant](repo:marshall/test/marshall/accounts/time_zones_property_test.exs) — Every curated zone over random instants 2000–2040 plus fixed DST edges; half-hour and 45-minute zones pinned.
- **property, present**: [difference is antisymmetric, zero on itself and its text follows the sign](repo:marshall/test/marshall/accounts/time_zones_property_test.exs) — Random zone pairs and instants; text direction and hour/minute spans.

## Give Windows guests an agent set with a capability table, reach a guest-side listener over virtio-vsock through the viosock driver, and make the fleet ready to stage the image

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: OverallsProtocol.GuestAgents names the closed agent set (linux, none, windows-v1) and a pure capability table; Lilly's jail, driver and executor and Marshall's per-capability image facts branch on the table, never on the set's name, so the agentless none row reproduces ADR-0170 exactly. The firmware jail gets the jail-local vsock endpoint only for an agent set that speaks the Lilly protocols. The readiness budget is the agent set's (600 s for windows-v1) and is recorded once per boot. The image ships the virtio-win viosock driver and, until the real agents exist, a SYSTEM probe that discovers the provider's address family at runtime, listens on vsock port 1099 and answers the host's CONNECT with one JSON line, publishing only its own log on the EFI system partition. Windows binaries are cross-built from the shared Lyra crate with the pinned zig toolchain; the Lyra gate type-checks the library and the Windows bins for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu. Images are configured as { path } objects; a size check decides template cacheability and every root disk is copied on demand (ADR-0177); both hosts' template budget is 96 GiB.

Required refusal: An unknown agent set string, a workspace source version 2 on an agentless manifest or a ninth manifest key is refused by the protocol; an older Lilly refuses a windows-v1 bundle, so the converged push precedes any placement. A missing, corrupt or mismatched manifest yields every capability false in Marshall. A bare image path or any image key beyond path, including the retired standby key, refuses Lilly's configuration. The probe carries no identity or credential material. The editor and the Inception profile stay refused for windows-v1.

Tested scope: Protocol tests pin the capability table and the windows-v1 manifest and bundle vectors; Lilly tests pin the agentless jail configuration, the vsock addition for windows-v1, the recorded readiness budget, the image configuration shape and template cacheability; Marshall tests bind the capabilities to the exact image ID for every agent set and exercise the per-capability surfaces; the windows-guest-unit evaluation checks the viosock driver, the agents directory, the probe task, the manifest arguments and the launcher's vsock device; the lyra check builds and type-checks the Windows target. Recorded on 2026-10-14: lyraWindows built overalls-winprobe.exe (PE32+, 320 000 bytes) through zig. The windows-guest machine test dials the probe through the launcher's vsock socket after the SAC prompt and reads its published log. The agents composition now also inspects the live Windows EFI log for the closed agentd startup line; this is present evidence only until the composed check runs. The staged Windows editor runtime and source recipes retain editor_capability=false; the editor-target-boundaries and windows-editor-runtime evaluations pass. The broker has 26 passing portable library and 7 Linux binary tests, Linux/Windows clippy and production Windows cross-link evidence. Thirty actual Windows library tests cover named-pipe timeout/cancellation and ACL descriptor/refusal checks; personal worker, task and browser lifecycle remain unrecorded. The separate editor candidate uses manifest v7/windows-editor-v1 and bundle v4 while this existing windows-v1 row remains editor false. The prior selected sealed e9ed22f1 image in live run 075200 reported ready while sshd was stopped and CLI SSH failed; that current failure is distinct from earlier dated fleet proofs.

## Build the Windows Server 2025 evaluation image offline and boot it under the patched Firecracker to the serial Special Administration Console

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: The image is installed inside a KVM Nix sandbox from Microsoft's hash-pinned evaluation ISO with restricted user networking and pinned virtio-win drivers; Firecracker boots the edk2 CloudHv firmware as a PVH payload over the opt-in virtio-pci transport. The patched VMM keeps its 1.16.1 identity and static linking; its seccomp surface widens by exactly one vCPU-thread ioctl (KVM_IOEVENTFD) for BAR relocation. This scenario covers the operator launcher only (no jailer, no host network guard); the Lilly launch path is the separate windows-lilly-guest-launch scenario.

Required refusal: The build fails without the OVERALLS-SETUP-COMPLETE serial marker and the firmware build fails without the PVH note or the patched aperture. The guest has a bootstrap Administrator credential and an interactive SAC login on serial, which must not be mistaken for the Linux console boundary. The manifest carries exactly the eight version-5 keys; a display name or any version-4 field is refused by the protocol.

Tested scope: Patched VMM identity, firmware provenance and offline assembly rules are checked without installing Windows; the nine VMM patches carry unit tests (PVH RSDP, PM timer, Hyper-V leaves, CMOS clock, BAR sizing and relocation with doorbell moves, virtio reset and re-activation, scatter-gather block requests on both I/O engines, vsock indirect descriptor tables). Recorded on 2026-10-13: the offline installation completed in about 255 seconds of guest time with all nine serial checkpoints, and the image booted under the patched Firecracker with both firmware variants to the Windows SAC prompt, answering `id` (OVERALLS, build 26100, Windows Server) and `i` (one virtio NIC). Recorded on 2026-10-14: the windows-guest machine test passed on nested KVM (firmware banner after 253 s of guest time, SAC> 6 s later, 274 s in total).

- **unit, present**: [Firecracker v1.16.1](repo:nix/verification/tests/evaluation/firecracker-vmm.nix) — The patched VMM reports the upstream version, lists --enable-pci and remains a static x86-64 firecracker/jailer pair; it does not boot a guest..
- **unit, present**: [disable-legacy=on](repo:nix/verification/tests/evaluation/windows-guest.nix) — Builder rules: KVM sandbox, restricted networking, modern-only virtio-pci, pinned ISO and drivers, EMS enabled, no autologon, version-5 manifest shape, launcher flags. No installation or boot..
- **machine, recorded**: [SAC>](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/windows-guest/driver.py) — Installs the evaluation image and boots it under the patched Firecracker on nested KVM until the Windows SAC prompt appears on the serial log. Firmware entry, ACPI, PM timer, virtio-blk-pci and EMS only; no networking or agents. Passed on 2026-10-14 (273.9 s script time).; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-14-windows-lilly-launch.md).

**Gaps:** No Marshall-driven Windows fleet matrix is recorded. The named image and nested KVM boot prove the operator and firmware paths only; WSL 2 and Podman nested virtualization, Hyper-V synthetic timers, SAC login and timekeeping under load remain unverified. Lilly launch, MMDS identity, agent trust/readiness, sparse template handling and Windows tools are covered by the linked scenarios.

**Preferred test work:** Add the Marshall-driven multi-OS fleet journey and record WSL 2, timekeeping and SAC security evidence; retain the operator-only boundary for this scenario.

## Place the Windows image through Lilly as a guest without agents and reach it on its delivered /32

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: The protocol admits exactly the eight-key version-5 manifest and the seven-key version-2 firmware bundle beside the unchanged version-4 and version-1 shapes; artifact names come from the protocol only. Lilly keeps rootfs.ext4 as the pool-side root slot, bind-mounts the firmware read-only, seeds the boot identity (placement, execution epoch, boot challenge, /32, gateway, MAC; never the generation) into Firecracker's MMDS from a root-owned jail-local metadata.json before launch, boots /firmware with the Hyper-V CPU template and --enable-pci, and runs the guest under the jailer, seccomp observation and the per-tap guard. The guest's SYSTEM bootstrap task reads MMDS with a V2 session token, validates every field including the adapter MAC and applies exactly the delivered /32. Marshall projects per-capability guest facts (guest_capabilities) from the immutable image, all service capabilities false for the agentless set.

Required refusal: A bundle with guest_agents none never reports guest_ready: trust is recorded as skipped for the exact boot, provisioning ends in the terminal unattested phase (no boot UUID, no path to ready), and readiness, terminal options, workspace sources and the Inception profile are refused before any host effect. Marshall refuses terminal sessions, agent turns, the agent executor binding, web search and Inception admission for such an image, hides the corresponding controls, and refuses new machine admission with git_identity_unavailable because agentless manifests cannot advertise the Git identity capability required by ADR-0198/0204. Physical-only measurement remains relevant to retained executions and the historical Lilly-only fixture. New admissions without Git identity support refuse with no allocation effects. An older Lilly fails closed on a firmware bundle, which is why the converged push precedes any placement. Lilly's host policy drops every unmarked packet between the host and a Customer guest, so nothing on the host reaches the Windows guest except the SSH and editor ingress paths it does not yet have. The guest bootstrap refuses an MMDS document whose fields fail validation or whose MAC is not the adapter's and never logs the token or boot challenge.

Tested scope: Protocol unit and property tests pin independent identity vectors for both manifest versions and the byte-identical version-1 bundle encoding; Lilly tests pin the kernel jail configuration and unit arguments unchanged and check the firmware variants, lifecycle edges (unattested, skipped) and firmware image loading; Marshall tests cover the capability property, admission refusal, service-level admission and hidden controls. The revised admission unit test passed within the focused run on 2026-10-19: agentless Git capability refusal allocates nothing; a Git-capable windows-v1 image admits physical and readiness measurements with its own budget. The retained pre-identity fixture checks physical-only measurement in its sandbox; this BEAM admission evidence does not update native launch acceptance. The windows-lilly-guest machine test drives the real Lilly driver on nested KVM: Inception refusal before any dataset, firmware bundle on the dataset with sparse usage, skipped trust and unattested provisioning from the journals, SAC> on the boot log, the guest's bootstrap log and applied identity read from the EFI system partition of the live disk without a login, ICMP and TCP 22 on the delivered /32 from Lilly's network namespace through a test-only accept for that address in the host policy (the tap guard stays intact and its accept counter is asserted), restart from the portable bundle without the image, stop and delete. Recorded on 2026-10-14: the windows-lilly-guest test passed end to end on nested KVM (2688 s).

- **property, present**: [identity survives serialization, changes with every bound input and never collides with v4](repo:protocol/test/image_manifest_test.exs) — Version-5 manifests round-trip, change identity with firmware bytes, root digest and minima, and never share an ID with a kernel manifest; the closed eight-key shape refuses names, kernels, editors and source versions. Pure codec evidence..
- **unit, present**: [firmware bundles boot the firmware over virtio-pci with MMDS identity and no vsock](repo:lilly/test/vm/jail_test.exs) — The firmware jail configuration and MMDS metadata document, and the unchanged kernel configuration. No real jail or KVM..
- **unit, present**: [an agentless boot reaches unattested with a challenge and can never become ready](repo:lilly/test/lifecycle/provisioning_test.exs) — Lifecycle edges for the unattested phase and the skipped trust state against the durable journal; no guest..
- **unit, recorded**: [firmware admissions require Git identity support while retained agentless VMs keep physical-only measurement](repo:marshall/test/marshall/compute/image_admission_test.exs) — Marshall registers agentless version-5 firmware, refuses Inception and ordinary Git-unsupported admission without VMs, operations, reservations or addresses, then inserts retained pre-identity state only in the sandbox and checks physical-only measurement. A windows-v1 manifest with explicit Git identity support retains SSH/terminal capability and no editor, and records physical plus readiness attempts with a 600-second readiness deadline. The focused admission cases passed; this database-backed BEAM evidence does not establish native guest acceptance.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-19-localization-feature-catalogs.md).
- **machine, recorded**: [the host reaches the guest through a test-only policy allowance; the tap guard is intact](repo:nix/verification/tests/machines/windows-lilly-guest/driver.py) — Real Lilly driver on nested KVM: firmware bundle, skipped trust, unattested provisioning, SAC> on the boot log, bootstrap log read from the live disk's EFI system partition, ICMP and TCP 22 on the delivered /32 through a test-only host-policy accept with the tap guard counted, restart from the bundle, delete. Passed on 2026-10-14 in 2688 s. No readiness, terminal or agent proof.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-14-windows-lilly-launch.md).

**Gaps:** Agentless launch is recorded. C: growth after a host-side extension and timekeeping under load remain unobserved; the host reachability probe is a test-only policy allowance, not a product path or Marshall observation. Agent trust/readiness, terminal, workspace, roster and executor coverage belongs to the windows-v1 scenario. Independent-host recovery and a repeatable Marshall-driven Windows matrix remain unverified.

**Preferred test work:** Add native growth/timekeeping and independent-host recovery evidence, then run the Marshall-driven multi-OS fleet journey.

## Stage and register the same sealed Windows installation on both hosts

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, isolation, storage, recovery.

Boundary: A recursive fixed-output Windows package binds exactly three dereferenced regular files, disk.raw, firmware and manifest.json, to reviewed NAR and manifest artifact pins with no store references. The shared fleet selector uses this package while the offline source installer remains independent. Existing signed-cache policy authenticates substitution; artifact identity grants no account access, execution capability, host isolation or storage mutation authority.

Required refusal: Missing publication refuses with operator guidance and exit 1, without reinstalling Windows, reading a host-local image, selecting different bytes or weakening signatures. A matching input-addressed installer path alone cannot establish identical Windows bytes. Manifest capabilities, authorization, current execution fences, guest isolation, storage ownership and recovery remain independent runtime checks.

Tested scope: Windows evaluation checks exact package/manifest pins, recursive hashing, empty allowedReferences, context-free fail-closed fallback and unique fleet selection, distinct from the source builder. Actual package resolution, exact three regular files, unchanged manifest, sizes/digests, no references and refusal-only fallback passed. Both hosts hold the exact reviewed recursive NAR identity with no references, imported the public cache signature and passed signature-required store verification. The matrix review and Windows guide retain exact identities. Actual lifecycle results retain separate scope.

- **unit, recorded**: [windows-fleet-sealed-selection](repo:nix/verification/tests/evaluation/windows-guest.nix) — Evaluated exact recursive pin, manifest/artifact descriptors, closed no-reference output, refusal fallback and shared fleet selector only; no installation, guest or live cache substitution.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).
- **manual, recorded**: [sha256-MTpVti0Mc+c3FzqjUJLfBAfEIW+plgP+HheZnVdPlUo=](repo:docs/guests/windows-guests.md) — Actual resolved sealed package has exact regular files, manifest/artifact bytes, reviewed NAR hash and no store references on both hosts. Public signed cache publication and signature-required verification passed independently of runtime acceptance.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).

**Gaps:** Publication custody does not establish a fresh Windows boot, readiness, personal-account SSH, terminal, executor, stop/restart/delete, physical deletion, crash/power-loss recovery or fleet availability. No generated artifact-substitution histories or isolated cache-outage machine test are recorded for this selector.

**Preferred test work:** Run a NixOS machine journey that substitutes the exact signed package in a fresh store, refuses missing/changed publication and then exercises the selected Windows lifecycle; add generated malformed manifest/custody histories without relaxing image identity.

## Complete Windows SSH bootstrap before ordinary key delivery and withhold readiness when bootstrap evidence is missing

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, execution, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Bootstrap-bound roster and host-certificate routes retain their existing fences. A new boot stops sshd, clears only regular direct entries in the managed key directory and requires a verified current-boot host certificate before starting its keyless listener and publishing the bootstrap receipt. Every readiness poll requires both current receipts and a live service. Ordinary key delivery still requires the running execution's completed provision/start operation. Account activation verifies the SID-bound registered profile after the MAX_PATH-bounded native API call; same-boot retries preserve current keys.

Required refusal: Missing, stale or unreadable bootstrap/certificate receipts, service probe errors, failed profile registration, reparse points, unexpected key directories and failed cleanup withhold bootstrap/readiness. Bootstrap never authorizes the ordinary key route before completed start. A denied key fetch does not erase current-boot keys or retract a completed keyless bootstrap.

Tested scope: The frozen Lyra gate passed 223 portable tests with Linux Clippy, Windows all-binary type checks and FreeBSD/illumos checks and Clippy. Actual shared readiness-answer cases cover absent/stale receipts, stopped/erroring services and foreign peers. The production bootstrap coordinator is tested with an ordinary-key fixture denied until completed start, stale-key cleanup refusal and same-boot preservation. Two isolated mutants, retaining prior keys and allowing readiness without a marker, were caught. A separate native CreateProfile diagnostic reproduced the 4096-unit RPC failure and successful 260-unit SID registration in the owned disposable old-image fixture; the old agent then enabled the account and started sshd. That fixture was mutated and is not an unchanged-image lifecycle pass. The repaired exact 8ca0a11f image then passed actual installation in 1,834.2 seconds and immutable NTFS readback of all three repaired executables; sealed no-reference NAR custody is recorded separately. Signed cache publication and exact NAR-fingerprint Ed25519 verification also passed; independent fresh Dungarees substitution, full NAR content verification, manifest/canonical identity and whole disk/firmware hashes then passed. Source selection pins those exact reviewed bytes; deployment and fresh runtime remain pending.

- **unit, recorded**: [new_boot_clears_stale_authority_before_listener_and_ordinary_keys](repo:lyra/src/guest/ssh_bootstrap.rs) — Actual production coordinator and shared readiness answer with controlled OS effects and a completed-start key-route fixture; no Windows APIs or physical execution.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).
- **unit, recorded**: [absent_or_stale_ssh_receipts_withhold_ready_even_when_sshd_runs](repo:lyra/src/bin/overalls-readinessd.rs) — Actual shared readiness predicate and answer with controlled current-marker and service results; no native marker, SCM or listener execution.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).
- **manual, recorded**: [MAX_PATH](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md) — Owned disposable fixture native CreateProfile comparison: 4096 units fail with Win32 1783; 260 units register the profile, after which the old agent progresses. Fixture mutated; no repaired-image lifecycle acceptance.; [execution record](repo:docs/architecture/reviews/2026-10-18-guest-os-matrix.md).

**Gaps:** Portable coordinator tests do not execute Windows SCM, profile creation or network listeners. Actual installation/readback establishes the repaired image bytes, not its physical lifecycle. Selected-image deployment and fresh exact-image create, strict CLI SSH, stop/restart/repeated SSH and cleanup remain separate. Scheduled-task crash recovery, hostile filesystem races and physical isolation remain unproven.

**Preferred test work:** Add a repeatable NixOS machine test driving the real Windows tasks through new-boot stale keys, denied ordinary key delivery before completed start, certificate replacement, profile API failure and same-boot recovery. Retain full exact-image live lifecycle results separately from that machine scope.

## Install the overalls CLI on a Windows workstation from the machine page and SSH into Linux and Windows guests through Audi

Coverage: **partial**. Layers: identity, authorization, transport, storage, recovery.

Boundary: Marshall serves /bin/install.ps1 templated with the deployment's SSH host trust (503 without it) and the windows-amd64 artifact with its SHA-256 digest from the same manifest as the Unix targets. The installer validates origin, zone and host against the issued values, requires an OpenSSH client with hostname protection (9.6+), installs Microsoft.OpenSSH.Preview with winget without asking when %ProgramFiles%\OpenSSH lacks one, and with one administrator approval places %ProgramFiles%\OpenSSH before the in-box 9.5 directory in the machine PATH (resolved in the elevated process; declined elevation leaves the machine PATH unchanged and points to overalls ssh) so the machine page shows one ssh HOST command, verifies the digest, runs config-ssh --staged-installer with the downloaded binary before installing it, and connects with overalls ssh through the recorded client. The managed SSH block quotes ProxyCommand as one double-quoted absolute path because Win32-OpenSSH runs it without a shell. Updates use the same digest manifest and activate by renaming the running executable aside.

Required refusal: A non-https origin, a foreign management host or zone, or a host outside the zone is refused before any download; a digest mismatch or failed SSH configuration leaves the installed binary and SSH profile unchanged; a client without hostname protection stops setup; an executable path containing a double quote is refused for ProxyCommand.

Tested scope: Rust unit tests pin Windows ProxyCommand quoting, the windows-amd64 target name and the portable UTC date; the Lyra Nix check type-checks the overalls binary for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu; the release publishes a PE32+ windows-amd64 artifact in the manifest; a Nix check parses install.ps1 with PowerShell and pins its refusals; Marshall tests cover /bin/install.ps1 templating and the machine page's Windows section.

- **unit, present**: [windows_proxy_command_is_one_double_quoted_path](repo:lyra/src/ssh_config.rs) — ProxyCommand quoting for Win32-OpenSSH: one double-quoted path, percent doubled, quotes and control characters refused; no SSH client runs..
- **unit, present**: [PowerShell installer is deployment bound, verifies the digest and gates OpenSSH 9.6](repo:marshall/test/marshall_web/controllers/overalls_controller_test.exs) — Marshall renders /bin/install.ps1 with the deployment host and zone, no-store and without cookies, and refuses it without trust; no PowerShell runs..
- **unit, present**: [origin does not match this installer](repo:nix/verification/tests/overalls-install-ps1.nix) — PowerShell parses the installer and it refuses bad origins, hosts and zones before any network access; no Windows host or OpenSSH..

**Gaps:** No execution on a real Windows workstation yet: unattended winget OpenSSH installation, the elevated machine PATH reordering and its declined-elevation fallback, config-ssh against Porsche, overalls ssh into Linux and Windows guests, overalls open and an update activation by rename-aside are unexercised; the planned proof uses a Windows Server 2025 fleet VM as the workstation.

**Preferred test work:** Run the page's PowerShell command on a Windows Server 2025 fleet VM, connect to a Linux and a Windows guest, and observe an update activation; record it in the review.
